news.exam_corner_topic: Shivakumar alleges ‘industrialist’ attempted sting op on him, Kerala CM using Meta glasses
news.headline: Shivakumar alleges ‘industrialist’ attempted sting op on him, Kerala CM using Meta glasses
news.story_lead: Shivakumar alleges ‘industrialist’ attempted sting op on him, Kerala CM using Meta glasses Shivakumar said he had documented the episode and had information about people who might have been involved. Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar has alleged that an industrialist who met him wearing Meta smart glasses was attempting to record a political conversation as part of a sting operation targeting him and Kerala chief minister VD Satheesan, both Congress leaders. Shivakumar said the visitor had obtained an appointment through officials and initially discussed business before turning to politics, including booth-level strategies and political developments.
news.full_article_text: Shivakumar alleges ‘industrialist’ attempted sting op on him, Kerala CM using Meta glasses Shivakumar said he had documented the episode and had information about people who might have been involved. Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar has alleged that an industrialist who met him wearing Meta smart glasses was attempting to record a political conversation as part of a sting operation targeting him and Kerala chief minister VD Satheesan, both Congress leaders. Shivakumar said the visitor had obtained an appointment through officials and initially discussed business before turning to politics, including booth-level strategies and political developments. The glasses, he said, made him suspicious. Also read: Rahul Gandhi ignited enthusiasm among youth: Shashi Tharoor after PM Modi's ‘failed product’ remark Shivakumar told a Kannada broadcaster that he asked officials to examine the visitor's background. He alleged that the information gathered showed the industrialist had also worn the glasses during a meeting with Satheesan , but not during meetings with Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu , Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis or a Union minister. “He wore the Meta glasses only when he came to me and VD Satheesan,” Shivakumar said. Shivakumar did not name the industrialist or provide evidence establishing that the glasses were used to record either meeting. He said authorities had taken precautionary measures but were withholding details. “Who said action wasn't sought? You just don't know, that's all. We are not disclosing it, that's all. We have taken all precautionary measures,” he said. Also read: TVK-led bloc, DMK walk out of ECI meeting in Tamil Nadu, seek CEC’s resignation He said he also cautioned his cabinet colleagues against attempts to entrap them through people working around them, telephone calls or other means. “As the head of the government, which is like a family, I have to tell the Cabinet ministers to be conscious and not get fooled,” he said. Shivakumar said he had documented the episode and had information about people who might have been involved, but would wait before disclosing their names or records. “I have called them all and kept records. Not now. When the time comes, I will say what has to be said. This is not the time to speak,” he said. The allegation comes as the Congress in Karnataka and opposition parties are locked in a dispute over purported sting operation videos involving former chief minister Siddaramaiah. The parties have exchanged allegations over the origin and purpose of the recordings. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Arun Dev Arun Dev is an Assistant Editor with the Karnataka bureau of Hindustan Times. A journalist for over 10 years, he has written extensively on crime and politics.

news.exam_corner_topic: Govt to issue consultation paper on a new AI law in ‘coming weeks’: Ashwini Vaishnaw
news.headline: Govt to issue consultation paper on a new AI law in ‘coming weeks’: Ashwini Vaishnaw
news.story_lead: Govt to issue consultation paper on a new AI law in ‘coming weeks’: Ashwini Vaishnaw Union minister Ashwini Vaishnav said the time has come when the risks of AI have crossed a threshold when we should come up with a law. Union minister for railways, information and broadcasting, and electronics and information technology Ashwini Vaishnaw on Friday said the government will issue a consultation paper on a new Artificial Intelligence (AI) law “in coming weeks”, saying the risks from the technology have crossed a “threshold” that now demands legislation. Speaking at the NDTV World Summit in Delhi, Vaishnaw said the proposed regulation will target the harms of AI while keeping humans in control of the technology.
news.full_article_text: Govt to issue consultation paper on a new AI law in ‘coming weeks’: Ashwini Vaishnaw Union minister Ashwini Vaishnav said the time has come when the risks of AI have crossed a threshold when we should come up with a law. Union minister for railways, information and broadcasting, and electronics and information technology Ashwini Vaishnaw on Friday said the government will issue a consultation paper on a new Artificial Intelligence (AI) law “in coming weeks”, saying the risks from the technology have crossed a “threshold” that now demands legislation. Speaking at the NDTV World Summit in Delhi, Vaishnaw said the proposed regulation will target the harms of AI while keeping humans in control of the technology. Also read: Rahul Gandhi ignited enthusiasm among youth: Shashi Tharoor after PM Modi's ‘failed product’ remark “Today the time has come when the risks of AI have crossed a threshold when we should come up with a law,” Vaishnaw said. “We should come up with a new regulation where the harms from the new technology can be regulated. Having said that, we are already working on it.” Why the shift on AI matters The remarks mark a visible shift in the government’s public stance. The IT ministry’s India AI Governance Guidelines, released on November 5, 2025, called for focused amendments to existing laws instead of a standalone AI statute. The ministry’s secretary S Krishnan said in December 2025 that no dedicated AI law was being planned, and a 2023 parliamentary reply under Vaishnaw said the government was not considering a law to regulate AI’s growth. Also read: TVK-led bloc, DMK walk out of ECI meeting in Tamil Nadu, seek CEC’s resignation The shift matters because the government has so far argued that existing laws and voluntary norms are enough, a position that critics said left gaps on risks such as autonomous agents and accountability. A consultation paper will be the first formal step towards a statute. Vaishnaw, a BJP leader, did not say when a bill could reach Parliament, and he gave no details on its scope, the regulator or penalties. Vaishnaw said that two schools of thought on AI exist globally. One argues that the technology should evolve sufficiently before it is regulated. The other, which he described as the European approach, is to “swat” every innovation early, a style he said stifles growth. “Our bias has always been towards more towards innovation,” Vaishnaw said, adding that the state must “simultaneously” keep citizens safe. The line suggests the proposed law will be framed as a harm-based regulation and not a licensing regime, though the government has not spelt out the design. The minister argued that no single country can write rules for a borderless technology. “In the digital world, the physical boundaries do not exist,” he said, adding that any initiative “has to be globally aligned”. He pointed to the nuclear industry, where countries sat together and agreed on principles that now govern the sector, as the template for AI. Vaishnaw said India will sit at that table as one of the “top three or top four AI ecosystems in the world”, along with the other global giants. The race towards innovation, he said, “has to be moderated by safety of human beings”. Some principles, he added, are already established. Those principles, in his words, are that AI “has to be human first” and “humancentric”. Control over the agents, the models, the outcomes and the processes “has to be in human hands”, he said, and there must be “some equivalent of stopping things if they go out of control”. The remarks echo concerns about AI agents acting without oversight, though he did not say how such a stopping mechanism will be mandated or who will hold the switch. Those questions are likely to be central to the consultation. On process, Vaishnaw said the paper will seek inputs from civil society, citizens, industry and other stakeholders. Banks, manufacturers, insurers and service firms are adopting AI rapidly, he said, so there is “a good understanding” of what the technology can deliver and what harm it can do. “We have discussed a lot with the tech companies,” he said. “Now we need to discuss with the stakeholders who are users of AI.” The shift in focus from developers to users is significant, since sectors such as banking and insurance are where AI errors can hit citizens directly. - Artificial Intelligence

news.headline: TN school principal, teacher, 2 students booked after Class 11 Dalit boy found dead in Coimbatore
news.story_lead: TN school principal, teacher, 2 students booked after Class 11 Dalit boy found dead in Coimbatore Tamil Nadu police have booked a school principal, a teacher and two students after a Class 11 Dalit boy was found dead in Coimbatore, amid caste harassment allegations. Tamil Nadu police have booked a school principal, a teacher and two students for alleged abetment to suicide after a Class 11 Dalit student was found dead at his home in Coimbatore, with his parents alleging that he was harassed over his caste and for consuming beef. All four accused have been detained, and the principal and the teacher have been suspended, police said.
news.full_article_text: TN school principal, teacher, 2 students booked after Class 11 Dalit boy found dead in Coimbatore Tamil Nadu police have booked a school principal, a teacher and two students after a Class 11 Dalit boy was found dead in Coimbatore, amid caste harassment allegations. Tamil Nadu police have booked a school principal, a teacher and two students for alleged abetment to suicide after a Class 11 Dalit student was found dead at his home in Coimbatore, with his parents alleging that he was harassed over his caste and for consuming beef. All four accused have been detained, and the principal and the teacher have been suspended, police said. The boy was found dead at his residence on October 21 in Peelamedu in Coimbatore. His parents have alleged that he was targeted by his class teacher and two classmates for belonging to the Scheduled Caste and for consuming beef, a police officer said. “We have lodged a case against the class teacher, school’s principal and two classmates for abetment to suicide under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 (abetment to suicide),” an officer said. The victim’s father works with a private hotel in Kerala and his mother is a domestic help in the Peelamedu locality of Coimbatore. According to the complaint by the parents, the accused teacher recently asked students from the Scheduled Caste community to stand up in the class and asked whether they consumed beef. “The boy admitted that he consumed beef,” the officer said, quoting the parents’ complaint. The officer added that the confession led to harassment of the boy by his classmates. On Friday, the victim’s father protested outside the Coimbatore district collectorate, demanding justice for his son. “How does it matter to the teacher whether I eat beef or curry. We want justice,” he told reporters. Allies of the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) also demanded justice for the victim and the arrest of the accused. Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) leader Thol Thirumavalavan said, “Let us all raise our voice for justice in relation to the suicide of a student in Coimbatore.” “All those responsible for the death of the student must be arrested. The government must form the social justice student force in every school**,”** he said in a party statement on Friday**.** Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president B Manickam Tagore said that in the land of social justice, there should not be even the slightest room for such toxic casteist thoughts in educational institutions. “The investigation must be completed quickly to ensure appropriate punishment for everyone involved,” he demanded. CPI (M) state secretary P Shanmugam said a teacher, who should be teaching that “all lives are born equal”, had humiliated the student on the basis of his caste. He claimed that even after a complaint was lodged against the teacher, the headmaster failed to intervene. Discussing suicides can be triggering for some. However, suicides are preventable. news.exam_corner_topic: Satellite-tagged Amur falcons complete round-trip migration across 23 countries, return to Manipur
news.headline: Satellite-tagged Amur falcons complete round-trip migration across 23 countries, return to Manipur
news.story_lead: Satellite-tagged Amur falcons complete round-trip migration across 23 countries, return to Manipur Satellite-tagged Amur falcons Apapang and Alang have returned to Manipur after covering nearly 20,000 km across 23 countries on their round-trip migration. After travelling across 23 countries and covering nearly 20,000 km, two satellite-tagged Amur falcons, Apapang and Alang, have returned to Manipur, completing a round-trip migration that included a six-day, non-stop flight of nearly 6,000 km between northeast India and Somalia in Africa, Union environment ministry officials said on Friday. The birds, which were tagged by Wildlife Institute of India scientists in November 2025, arrived from China on Thursday and are expected to spend the next two to three weeks at selected sites in the mountainous tracts of Tamenglong district before embarking on their next long-haul flight.
news.full_article_text: Satellite-tagged Amur falcons complete round-trip migration across 23 countries, return to Manipur Satellite-tagged Amur falcons Apapang and Alang have returned to Manipur after covering nearly 20,000 km across 23 countries on their round-trip migration. After travelling across 23 countries and covering nearly 20,000 km, two satellite-tagged Amur falcons, Apapang and Alang, have returned to Manipur, completing a round-trip migration that included a six-day, non-stop flight of nearly 6,000 km between northeast India and Somalia in Africa, Union environment ministry officials said on Friday. The birds, which were tagged by Wildlife Institute of India scientists in November 2025, arrived from China on Thursday and are expected to spend the next two to three weeks at selected sites in the mountainous tracts of Tamenglong district before embarking on their next long-haul flight. Manipur, along with other parts of northeast India, serves as an important stopover for the migratory birds, which feed on termites to accumulate fat reserves for their next leg of the journey — a nearly 6,000-km flight to Somalia, including a 3,000-km crossing over the Arabian Sea. Apapang and Alang, along with a third falcon named Ahu, were fitted with satellite transmitters by scientists from the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) at the Chiuluan roosting site in Tamenglong district in November 2025. While tracking signals from Apapang and Alang confirmed their return to Manipur, scientists lost contact with Ahu somewhere in Somalia earlier this year. “The two Amur falcons are expected to now make a two to three week stopover at select sites in the beautiful mountainous tracts of Tamenglong district in Manipur, where local people now eagerly wait for their return year after year and protect the falcons,” environment minister Bhupender Yadav said in a post on X on Friday. Yadav said the successful completion of the birds’ full round-trip journey marked an important milestone. “The two Amur falcons are expected to now make a two to three week stopover at select sites in the beautiful mountainous tracts of Tamenglong district in Manipur, where local people now eagerly wait for their return year after year and protect the falcons,” said Yadav on X. Amur falcons typically spend their winter in southern Africa, reaching there between November and December and staying until March or April before returning to their breeding grounds in northern China and Siberia by April and May. They are primarily insectivores, feeding on termites, ants, locusts and beetles, but can also consume mice, smaller birds and lizards. Officials at the Union environment ministry said the Amur falcon tracking project began in 2013, initially in Nagaland, as a conservation effort to address the issue of hunting at stopover sites in northeast India. Ramesh Pandey, additional director general of forests at the environment ministry, said that, with the active participation of local people, the project provides unique insights into the species, particularly their non-stop, long-distance flights of nearly 6,000 km in six days from northeast India to Somalia. “With the falcons returning back a year later and few making round-trip journeys multiple times to the stopover sites in Nagaland, this created the desired awareness among local people and a sense of ownership began. This also resulted in hunters turning protectors, leading to complete protection of this migratory falcon,” he said. Pandey said that, to continue the conservation efforts, another phase of satellite tagging was carried out in 2016 across stopover sites in Nagaland. The success of the initiative spread to neighbouring Manipur and Assam, where Amur falcons began to receive protection at the stopover sites as well. Amur falcons have been tagged in 2019, 2024 and 2025, with the latest tagging taking place in November 2025, when three such falcons were tagged in Manipur. “The successful tracking of Amur falcons has provided much needed information on where and how long they stop over in northeast India, and also as to how super-abundant termite prey availability in and around the stopover sites has shaped their migration strategies,” Pandey said. He added that in southern Africa, in the southern hemisphere, the Amurs spend nearly three months during the southern summer in Botswana, Zimbabwe and South Africa. Similarly, their breeding sites in northeastern China and the Russian Far East are also well mapped, he said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Jasjeev Gandhiok Jasjeev Gandhiok is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times, where he covers environment, climate change, the clean energy transition and wildlife at the National Bureau. Gandhiok has over a decade of experience in journalism and is based in Delhi. He has reported extensively on Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR). This includes the region's air pollution woes, a polluted Yamuna and on urban wildlife still thriving in the region. He joined HT in October 2021. Prior to that, he had five-year stint at The Times of India in Delhi, where he also covered Delhi, with a focus on environment and wildlife. Gandhiok has covered some recent events around the Capital too, ranging from the farmers' protests, the northeast Delhi riots and the CAA-NRC protests, reporting from the ground on all of these. He also travels across the country to report on how environment and climate change impact everyday life, while also writing on endangered species. His reports in 2019 on toxic leachate from Delhi's landfills led to the National Green Tribunal (NGT) taking suo motu cognisance and ultimately asking the state government to start bio-mining to flatten and remove all three landfills in the capital. He also closely tracks the implementation of government policies on climate, renewable energy and environmental protection. His focus remains on impactful, public-interest journalism which explains how environmental decisions affect people's everyday lives. Read More

The birds, which were tagged by Wildlife Institute of India scientists in November 2025, arrived from China on Thursday and are expected to spend the next two to three weeks at selected sites in the mountainous tracts of Tamenglong district before embarking on their next long-haul flight.

Manipur, along with other parts of northeast India, serves as an important stopover for the migratory birds, which feed on termites to accumulate fat reserves for their next leg of the journey — a nearly 6,000-km flight to Somalia, including a 3,000-km crossing over the Arabian Sea.

Apapang and Alang, along with a third falcon named Ahu, were fitted with satellite transmitters by scientists from the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) at the Chiuluan roosting site in Tamenglong district in November 2025. While tracking signals from Apapang and Alang confirmed their return to Manipur, scientists lost contact with Ahu somewhere in Somalia earlier this year.

“The two Amur falcons are expected to now make a two to three week stopover at select sites in the beautiful mountainous tracts of Tamenglong district in Manipur, where local people now eagerly wait for their return year after year and protect the falcons,” environment minister Bhupender Yadav said in a post on X on Friday.
Yadav said the successful completion of the birds’ full round-trip journey marked an important milestone.

news.headline: India Records Best-Ever Medal Haul at Asian Para Games, Finishes Fourth in Standings
news.story_lead: India completed its most successful campaign in Asian Para Games history, securing fourth place in the overall medal standings with 114 medals, including 30 gold medals. China dominated the event, taking the top spot ahead of Japan and Uzbekistan.
news.full_article_text:
Asian Para Games: Performance Breakdown

India concluded its Asian Para Games campaign with its highest-ever medal tally, finishing 4th in the overall standings with 30 gold, 35 silver, and 49 bronze medals, bringing the total count to 114. 

Top Nations in Asian Para Games Medal Tally:
- 1. China: 204 Gold, 115 Silver, 108 Bronze (Total: 427)
- 2. Japan: 63 Gold, 60 Silver, 62 Bronze (Total: 185)
- 3. Uzbekistan: 45 Gold, 49 Silver, 51 Bronze (Total: 145)
- 4. India: 30 Gold, 35 Silver, 49 Bronze (Total: 114)
- 5. South Korea: 28 Gold, 36 Silver, 33 Bronze (Total: 97)
- 6. Iran: 26 Gold, 36 Silver, 40 Bronze (Total: 102)
- 7. Thailand: 18 Gold, 39 Silver, 63 Bronze (Total: 120)
- 8. Indonesia: 14 Gold, 20 Silver, 37 Bronze (Total: 71)
- 9. Kazakhstan: 12 Gold, 16 Silver, 22 Bronze (Total: 50)
- 10. Saudi Arabia: 8 Gold, 8 Silver, 1 Bronze (Total: 17)

Key Athletes and Milestone Performances:
- Javelin thrower Sumit Antil led an Indian 1-2-3 podium sweep in the men's event.
- Mona Agarwal created history by becoming the first Indian athlete to earn an Asian Para Games medal in the 50m rifle 3 positions event. She was also selected alongside Nishad Kumar as India's flag-bearers for the closing ceremony.
- Thulasimathi Murugesan capped her campaign with three medals in a single day, including a gold in para-badminton.
- Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi secured the gold medal in the men's recurve doubles archery event.
- Swimmer Himanshu Nandal earned three bronze medals during the tournament.

news.headline: High Inflation Functions Like a Universal Tax: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra at NDTV World Summit
news.story_lead: Speaking at the NDTV World Summit, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated that elevated inflation acts like an indirect tax affecting everyone across society. The observation emphasizes the broader economic burden caused by rising price levels on household purchasing power.
news.full_article_text:
### RBI Governor on the Burden of Inflation

Addressing the NDTV World Summit, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra highlighted the systemic impact of elevated price levels on the public. He pointed out that sustained price increases reduce purchasing power, acting effectively as a broad tax on citizens.

* **Event:** NDTV World Summit 2026
* **Key Speaker:** Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra
* **Main Observation:** High inflation functions similarly to a universal tax on everyone due to its widespread impact on real income.
bullet_points: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra addressed participants at the NDTV World Summit 2026.
He stated that high inflation operates similarly to a tax on everyone in society.
The remark highlights the severe impact of elevated inflation on real consumer purchasing power.
Maintaining price stability remains a central objective for monetary policy management.
key_facts: Speaker: Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra
Forum: NDTV World Summit 2026
Key Observation: High inflation acts like a tax on everyone
Date: October 23, 2026
important_dates: 2026-10-23: Address by RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra at the NDTV World Summit
exam_relevance: Prelims: General awareness of monetary terms, macroeconomic indicators, and central bank functions.
Mains: GS Paper III (Indian Economy, inflation management, and monetary policy objectives).
news.upsc_analysis: Inflation acts as an implicit regressive burden on consumers by lowering the real value of currency. Monetary policy mechanisms seek to anchor price stability to protect disposable incomes and sustain balanced macroeconomic expansion.
impacts: Erosion of real purchasing power across all demographics.
way_forward: Balancing price stability and macroeconomic growth objectives through prudent monetary management.
news.mains_notes:
**Topic: Inflation and Monetary Management (GS Paper III)**

* **Economic Burden:** Inflation serves as a hidden burden on households by reducing real disposable income.
* **Monetary Policy Role:** Central bank price stability mandates aim to mitigate inflationary impacts on the overall economy.
mains_questions: "High inflation acts as an unannounced tax on society." Discuss this statement in the context of Indian macroeconomic management and central banking policy.
Examine the mechanisms used by central banks to maintain price stability while fostering sustainable economic growth.
news.takeaway: At the NDTV World Summit, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra noted that high inflation acts as a universal tax on all citizens by diminishing purchasing power.

hindi_translation.headline: उच्च मुद्रास्फीति हर किसी पर कर की तरह है: एनडीटीवी वर्ल्ड समिट में आरबीआई गवर्नर संजय मल्होत्रा
hindi_translation.story_lead: एनडीटीवी वर्ल्ड समिट को संबोधित करते हुए भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक (आरबीआई) के गवर्नर संजय मल्होत्रा ने कहा कि उच्च मुद्रास्फीति समाज के सभी लोगों को प्रभावित करने वाले एक अप्रत्यक्ष कर की तरह काम करती है। यह टिप्पणी जनता की क्रय शक्ति पर बढ़ती कीमतों के व्यापक आर्थिक प्रभाव को रेखांकित करती है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### मुद्रास्फीति के बोझ पर आरबीआई गवर्नर

एनडीटीवी वर्ल्ड समिट को संबोधित करते हुए भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक (आरबीआई) के गवर्नर संजय मल्होत्रा ने जनता पर बढ़ती मूल्य दरों के प्रभाव को रेखांकित किया। उन्होंने कहा कि निरंतर मूल्य वृद्धि क्रय शक्ति को कम करती है, जो नागरिकों पर एक व्यापक कर के रूप में काम करती है।

* **कार्यक्रम:** एनडीटीवी वर्ल्ड समिट 2026
* **मुख्य वक्ता:** भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक के गवर्नर संजय मल्होत्रा
* **मुख्य अवलोकन:** उच्च मुद्रास्फीति वास्तविक आय पर अपने व्यापक प्रभाव के कारण सभी पर एक सार्वभौमिक कर की तरह काम करती है।
bullet_points: आरबीआई गवर्नर संजय मल्होत्रा ने एनडीटीवी वर्ल्ड समिट 2026 को संबोधित किया।
उन्होंने कहा कि उच्च मुद्रास्फीति समाज में हर व्यक्ति पर एक कर की तरह काम करती है।
यह टिप्पणी उपभोक्ताओं की वास्तविक क्रय शक्ति पर मुद्रास्फीति के प्रभाव को दर्शाती है।

news.headline: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds
news.story_lead: Watch: Doctors told the BBC about the targeting of Sudanese hospitals - Published 23 October 2026, 00:16 BST A BBC investigation has found evidence that Sudanese paramilitary fighters systematically destroyed el-Fasher's healthcare system during their long siege and subsequent takeover of the city in Darfur a year ago. UN human rights chief Volker TÃ¼rk called the findings "deeply disturbing", saying multiple attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on civilian infrastructure, including health facilities, were serious violations of international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes. The RSF has rejected the BBC's findings.
news.full_article_text: Watch: Doctors told the BBC about the targeting of Sudanese hospitals - Published 23 October 2026, 00:16 BST A BBC investigation has found evidence that Sudanese paramilitary fighters systematically destroyed el-Fasher's healthcare system during their long siege and subsequent takeover of the city in Darfur a year ago. UN human rights chief Volker TÃ¼rk called the findings "deeply disturbing", saying multiple attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on civilian infrastructure, including health facilities, were serious violations of international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes. The RSF has rejected the BBC's findings. The health minister of the group's civilian-affiliated government dismissed the allegations as propaganda. Dr Alaa Eldin Nugud said it was a deliberate attempt by the national army and its allies to smear the RSF's reputation. Using sources who were on the ground in el-Fasher, the BBC has found details of at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and healthcare sites from May 2024 to October 2025 - some hit multiple times. Under international law it is illegal to attack health facilities or their staff during conflict. The investigation also reveals the toll on medical workers in the western city. In the period from April 2023 to October 2025, the BBC's data shows 120 were injured, 55 killed and 10 forcibly "disappeared" or abducted. "The RSF [were] trying to evacuate the hospitals, to put them out of service because the health system is the cornerstone of any city or any state," says Dr Muhamed Suliman, a surgeon who was based in el-Fasher during the siege and spoke to the BBC. "The RSF started hitting these areas so citizens have no longer any way to stay there. It was intense. It was deliberate. It was planned." The investigation comes a year after the fall of el-Fasher, one of the most brutal chapters of the civil war which erupted in April 2023 between the RSF and Sudan's military. Both sides have been accused of attacks on health facilities. El-Fasher residents had little access to healthcare during the long siege of the city In March 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) condemned the bombing of al-Daein hospital in RSF-held eastern Darfur, which killed dozens and forced the site to close. Sudan's military is believed to have carried out the drone strikes, although it has denied responsibility. But events in el-Fasher represent "one of the clearest and most severe examples of the wider impact of the conflict on health care in Sudan," the WHO said in response to a BBC query. UN investigators have reported that the fighting in el-Fasher bore the "hallmarks of genocide", where historical ethnic animosities have seen Arab militias - now the backbone of RSF forces - target non-Arab groups such as those that populate the city. The BBC's investigation reveals for the first time a detailed chronology of attacks on healthcare during the long siege of the city. - A simple guide to what is happening in Sudan Published 13 November 2025 - Reports of mass killings in Sudan have echoes of its dark past Published 31 October 2025 - Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say Published 2 days ago Some medical facilities in el-Fasher closed down within weeks of the country's civil war starting in April 2023. Crucially this included one of the main hospitals - the Teaching Hospital - located in a conflict zone in the middle of the city. Its operations were moved to el-Fasher's South Hospital. There medical services continued, although increasingly hindered by power cuts and dwindling supplies. The situation changed dramatically a year later, when the RSF mounted its siege of el-Fasher. In late May and early June of 2024, the South Hospital was shelled several times as paramilitary fighters pushed forward from their positions in the east of the city. The first bombing came as a shock, says Dr Suliman. The area around the hospital that was hit was "very crowded because it was the only working hospital in the city providing surgical services", he says. On that day medical staff operated on 16 injured patients, he added. The attacks culminated in an RSF raid on 8 June. Hospital staff were taken by surprise - many of them escaped over the back wall as the RSF fighters entered the building, says Dr Mustafa Ahmed, a pharmaceutical specialist. But the director general of the hospital, surgeon Izzeldin Ahmed Dawaud Asow, encountered a group of the paramilitaries outside his office. They did not know he was a doctor, he said, but denounced him with ethnic slurs. "There are no citizens here. You are Falangi," they said, using a derogatory term implying that non-Arab Sudanese are foreigners. Dr Asow says he was beaten with rifle butts and lost consciousness at one point. Ultimately, he saved himself by pretending to be dead. "They put their hand on my chest, and I stopped breathing. And they said: 'Leave him, leave him. The rubbish has died. Leave him.' They left me." That same day the RSF was driven out by the Sudanese military and its allies and Dr Asow returned to find the bodies of several patients and the surgical equipment in his operating room thoroughly destroyed, he said. The hospital closed and later fell into RSF hands when the army retreated. Dr Nugud, a prominent Sudanese surgeon who has joined the RSF-backed civilian government as health minister, insisted the South Hospital was being used as a military base. According to international law, hospitals can lose their protection if they are used by a party to the conflict to commit an "act harmful to the enemy". In an interview with the BBC, Dr Nugud declared that missile launchers were set up on the grounds and shared a video showing remains of weapons filmed more than a year after the hospital closed, which he said supported his claim. He also showed us what he called maps of landmines planted around the Teaching Hospital, which is located next to Sudanese military headquarters. Doctors told us the hospital was not incorporated into the base and said they visited it to pick up medical equipment during the war. The BBC has found no independent evidence of Dr Nugud's allegations. And the government of the Darfur region categorically rejected the charges. After the South Hospital shut, its staff and remaining equipment were moved to the Saudi Maternity Hospital in the west of the city, where the army had its main bases. "We do not know if hospitals are being intentionally targeted, butâ¦ the belligerents are not taking any precautions to spare them," it said in a statement. However, in the course of our investigation we spoke to six doctors who described a pattern of systematic targeting. news.headline: ‘Enough clean chits to China’: Mallikarjun Kharge, Congress questions PM Modi over security, trade

PM Modi must come clean before India!” Kharge said in a post on X, accusing the government of “keeping the nation in the dark” over border security.
news.full_article_text: ‘Enough clean chits to China’: Mallikarjun Kharge, Congress questions PM Modi over security, trade Kharge’s remarks came after ITBP chief Shatrujeet Kapoor said that face-offs with Chinese PLA troops were continuing along the Arunachal Pradesh border Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Friday questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi over India’s national and economic security in relation to China, citing reported ongoing face-offs between Indian and Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradesh and the widening trade deficit between the two countries. “Enough clean chits to China. PM Modi must come clean before India!” Kharge said in a post on X, accusing the government of “keeping the nation in the dark” over border security. Kharge’s remarks came after Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) director general Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor said on Friday that face-offs with Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA) troops were continuing at multiple locations along the Arunachal Pradesh border. The developments follow reports of face-offs in the Taksing area and Corps Commander-level talks held at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point to address tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC). In his post, Kharge referred to reports of Chinese incursions near Taksing in August and questioned whether India’s patrolling access had been compromised. He also asked whether the confrontations signalled the possibility of another serious border crisis after the Galwan clash in June 2020, in which 20 Indian Army personnel were killed. “Has India’s patrolling access been compromised? Arunachal Pradesh is an inseparable part of India. Why is the nation being kept in the dark?” Kharge questioned. Since July, there have been reports of a standoff with Chinese troops in the remote Taksin area of Upper Subansiri district. Asked about this in a press conference in August, foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the state of border affairs has ramifications for overall India-China ties, adding that the two sides have agreed to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to “avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation” along the border. Kharge's concern Raising concerns over India’s trade relationship with China , Kharge said, “Chinese imports have surged 102 per cent, while India's trade deficit with China has ballooned 155 per cent to $112.16 billion. Even Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman admits China obstructs Indian exports.” He questioned the government’s reported moves to ease investment restrictions and consider production-linked incentive (PLI) benefits for eligible China-linked ventures. “Has Make in India become Import from China?” he asked. Kharge also questioned the outcomes of India’s diplomatic engagements with Beijing, saying, “What tangible results have these engagements delivered? Have India’s pre-May 2020 patrolling rights been fully restored?” The government has in the past rejected the Congress's allegations of bowing down to Beijing, saying it was committed to protecting India's borders. At the same time, BJP functionaries have accused the Congress of politicising national security issues. They have also hit back at the opposition party, saying Jawaharlal Nehru ceded ground to China. India and China have attempted to rebuild their relationship after reaching an understanding in October 2024 to end a military standoff in Ladakh that lasted more than four years and took ties to a six-decade low. Chinese President Xi Jinping made his first visit to India in seven years to attend the BRICS Summit on September 12-13, and held a bilateral meeting with PM Modi to review ties. Speaking at an Asia Society event in New York in late September, external affairs minister S Jaishankar said India-China ties were better today than they were a couple of years ago. Congress criticism Congress criticised PM Modi for meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping at the BRICS summit while face-offs were reportedly ongoing along the Arunachal Pradesh border. Kharge, meanwhile, said national security demanded accountability rather than what he termed “diplomatic photo opportunities” and “Hugplomacy”. “Imagine—one side, China was clashing with our soldiers; on the other, Modi was welcoming China’s president. It’s like rubbing salt in the wounds of our soldiers,” the party said on their official X handle. “Sometimes giving China a clean chit, sometimes abandoning control of patrolling points and the country's land. This weak Prime Minister has caused immense damage to the country,” the party added.

news.headline: Fadnavis announces probe into viral clips linked to Maratha activist Jarange-Patil
news.story_lead: Fadnavis announces probe into viral clips linked to Maratha activist Jarange-Patil Fadnavis cited calls for an inquiry and said the forensic investigation will examine whose voices are in the clips Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Friday announced a forensic probe into the audio clips that Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange-Patil released a day earlier alleging a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) conspiracy to influence the political narrative ahead of the 2024 assembly elections. One clip features a woman purportedly claiming that ₹ 500 crore was paid to Jarange-Patil through Shiv Sena leader Shrikant Shinde to benefit the BJP electorally. Another purported BJP leader discusses the need to amplify “love jihad” cases to shape public opinion.
news.full_article_text: Fadnavis announces probe into viral clips linked to Maratha activist Jarange-Patil Fadnavis cited calls for an inquiry and said the forensic investigation will examine whose voices are in the clips Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Friday announced a forensic probe into the audio clips that Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange-Patil released a day earlier alleging a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) conspiracy to influence the political narrative ahead of the 2024 assembly elections. One clip features a woman purportedly claiming that ₹ 500 crore was paid to Jarange-Patil through Shiv Sena leader Shrikant Shinde to benefit the BJP electorally. Another purported BJP leader discusses the need to amplify “love jihad” cases to shape public opinion. The BJP has demanded a probe into whether the recordings were real or AI-generated. Fadnavis cited calls for an inquiry and said the forensic investigation will examine whose voices are in the recordings and evaluate the motives behind releasing them after two and a half years. He said the probe will reveal the complete truth. Fadnavis, who was in Nagpur to vote in the legislative council graduate constituency election, made the announcement when asked about the suspicious timing of the audio clips surfacing after two and a half years. He said an impartial inquiry will uncover the absolute truth. Jarange-Patil held a press conference in Jalna and played a 31-minute audio recording. He said the recording reveals a long-running political conspiracy spanning the last three years aimed at weakening the Maratha reservation movement and tarnishing his reputation. Jarange-Patil presented the clips as evidence and urged top leaders, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Fadnavis, and his deputy Eknath Shinde, to launch a thorough probe. Eknath Shinde denied the ₹ 500 crore bribery claims. Leaders of his Shiv Sena, including Sanjay Shirsat, Uday Samant, and Dada Bhuse, rejected all allegations as part of a smear campaign. They said the audio clips and politics around them were being used maliciously to defame Eknath Shinde and demanded an inquiry.

Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Friday announced a forensic probe into the audio clips that Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange-Patil released a day earlier alleging a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) conspiracy to influence the political narrative ahead of the 2024 assembly elections.

One clip features a woman purportedly claiming that ₹ 500 crore was paid to Jarange-Patil through Shiv Sena leader Shrikant Shinde to benefit the BJP electorally. Another purported BJP leader discusses the need to amplify “love jihad” cases to shape public opinion. The BJP has demanded a probe into whether the recordings were real or AI-generated.

Fadnavis cited calls for an inquiry and said the forensic investigation will examine whose voices are in the recordings and evaluate the motives behind releasing them after two and a half years. He said the probe will reveal the complete truth.

Fadnavis, who was in Nagpur to vote in the legislative council graduate constituency election, made the announcement when asked about the suspicious timing of the audio clips surfacing after two and a half years. He said an impartial inquiry will uncover the absolute truth.

news.headline: Keralam seeks extension of deadline for ration card e-KYC
news.story_lead: Keralam seeks extension of deadline for ration card e-KYC Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam Food and Civil Supplies Minister Anoop Jacob has urged the Centre to extend the three-month deadline for activating ration cards through e-KYC and defer the implementation of new provisions for temporarily cancelling cards unused for six consecutive months. In a letter to his counterpart at the Centre Pralhad Joshi, Jacob sought flexibility in implementing the 2025 amendment order to the Targeted Public Distribution System Order, which provides for temporary cancellation and subsequent verification of ration cards that have not been used for six months. The minister also sought permission for the state to maintain a waiting list of eligible families in the order of first-in, first-out to fill vacancies arising from the cancellation of cards, according to a statement issued by his office on Friday.
news.full_article_text: Keralam seeks extension of deadline for ration card e-KYC Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam Food and Civil Supplies Minister Anoop Jacob has urged the Centre to extend the three-month deadline for activating ration cards through e-KYC and defer the implementation of new provisions for temporarily cancelling cards unused for six consecutive months. In a letter to his counterpart at the Centre Pralhad Joshi, Jacob sought flexibility in implementing the 2025 amendment order to the Targeted Public Distribution System Order, which provides for temporary cancellation and subsequent verification of ration cards that have not been used for six months. The minister also sought permission for the state to maintain a waiting list of eligible families in the order of first-in, first-out to fill vacancies arising from the cancellation of cards, according to a statement issued by his office on Friday. He proposed that cards identified for removal could be temporarily shifted to or retained under the state's tide-over/non-priority category, subject to conditions. The entitlement to foodgrains under the National Food Security Act should not be withdrawn merely because a ration card has remained unused for a period, Jacob said. He said foodgrains can be provided under the state category whenever required, subject to Aadhaar-based biometric authentication. Eligibility can be reassessed through e-KYC and field verification within a specified period, and NFSA status can be restored if the beneficiary was found eligible, he pointed out. Such a system will help remove ineligible families while preventing genuine beneficiaries from being inadvertently excluded and ensuring that NFSA entitlements are availed of only by eligible people, he said. The minister said the first phase will affect 44,279 priority ration cardholders in Keralam, including 5,370 yellow-card and 38,909 pink-card holders, who had not purchased ration supplies for more than six months. The fact that these beneficiaries had not collected ration supplies for six months did not automatically make them ineligible, he said, adding that the reasons for their inactivity needed detailed examination, which will take time. Removing them immediately at this stage can therefore be unjust, Jacob said in the letter. He also pointed out that around 5,62,494 non-priority ration cardholders in the state had not purchased ration supplies for more than six months. These families continued under the state's tide-over arrangements and could obtain foodgrains whenever required through biometric authentication, he said. Retaining the cards will also help families during emergencies such as epidemics and natural disasters, when the absence of ration cards can cause hardship, the minister said. He cited the COVID-19 lockdown as an example, noting that even affluent families could access foodgrains through fair-price shops during the crisis. Jacob urged the Centre to permit the temporary shifting or retention of NFSA, Antyodaya Anna Yojana and Priority Household ration cards under the state's tide-over/non-priority category until field verification and reassessment of eligibility were completed. news.headline: 322 kg of ghee seized in Delhi after checks at stores offering huge discounts ahead of festive season
news.story_lead: 322 kg of ghee seized in Delhi after checks at stores offering huge discounts ahead of festive season The inspections focused on retailers promoting deals such as 'Buy One, Get One Free' and discounts of up to 60 per cent. The Delhi government's food safety department has confiscated more than 322 kg of ghee during inspections of shops offering steep discounts on social media ahead of the festive season, officials said on Friday. The action followed concerns over the quality and pricing of the products being sold.
news.full_article_text: 322 kg of ghee seized in Delhi after checks at stores offering huge discounts ahead of festive season The inspections focused on retailers promoting deals such as 'Buy One, Get One Free' and discounts of up to 60 per cent. The Delhi government's food safety department has confiscated more than 322 kg of ghee during inspections of shops offering steep discounts on social media ahead of the festive season, officials said on Friday. The action followed concerns over the quality and pricing of the products being sold. The inspections focused on retailers promoting deals such as 'Buy One, Get One Free' and discounts of up to 60 per cent. Officials checked whether the shops were following food safety regulations and took steps to prevent the sale of adulterated, substandard, expired or incorrectly labelled food products, news agency PTI reported. Ghee seized from three stores During inspections at Maxcart Store and Aggarwal Store in Vikaspuri, officials collected five enforcement samples of ghee from different brands and five samples of other food items. More than 75.50 litres of ghee was seized. In a separate inspection at Aggarwal Store in Hastal village, the team collected three enforcement samples of ghee sold under the Shri Shan, Vrinda Farms and Avtar brands. Officials seized 246 kg of ghee from the store. The department said the samples would be assessed alongside laboratory test reports before any further action is taken. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said in a statement issued on Friday that the government would not tolerate food adulteration or any irregularities that could endanger public health. She also advised consumers to examine food products carefully before buying them, including checking their quality, packaging, manufacturing dates and expiry dates. Food samples collected from shops across Delhi The department also carried out inspections at other establishments to check compliance with food safety and labelling requirements. At Sahib Sons in Azad Market, which operates under the trade name Vicon International, officials collected two samples of sugar-boiled confectionery over suspected labelling irregularities. Samples of makhana and turmeric powder were collected from Jain Store in Lajpat Nagar. At Yug Basket Private Limited in Rithala, officials took samples of two varieties of biscuits, soft candy and sugar-based candy. The department said violations of food safety requirements had been recorded at the inspected establishments and that further action would follow. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Shivya Kanojia Shivya Kanojia is a journalist at Hindustan Times, where she works in the fast-paced digital news ecosystem with a strong sense of editorial judgement and a clear understanding of what makes a story both important and traffic-driven. An alumna of the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC), Shivya brings a thoughtful balance of news value and audience relevance to her work, ensuring stories resonate beyond the immediate headline. Over the course of her three-year journey in the digital news space, Shivya has worked across a wide range of beats, including politics, civic issues, human-interest features and trending news. This diverse exposure has shaped her ability to approach stories with nuance, adaptability and context, whether she is breaking down complex developments or spotlighting everyday narratives that often go unnoticed. She is particularly drawn to human-interest stories, interviews and explainers that offer depth and clarity, aiming to move past surface-level reporting to explore the people, emotions and circumstances behind the news. Prior to joining Hindustan Times, Shivya worked with Firstpost and Times Now, where she covered a broad spectrum of topics and honed her skills in digital journalism . Outside the newsroom, Shivya enjoys discovering new cafés, drawn to good coffee, cosy spaces and unhurried conversations. Shopping is another pastime she cherishes, not always out of necessity, but often guided by instinct and the simple joy of stumbling upon unexpected finds. Above all, she treasures time spent with loved ones, finding meaning in shared laughter, simple moments and memories that linger long after. Read More

The Delhi government's food safety department has confiscated more than 322 kg of ghee during inspections of shops offering steep discounts on social media ahead of the festive season, officials said on Friday. The action followed concerns over the quality and pricing of the products being sold.

The inspections focused on retailers promoting deals such as 'Buy One, Get One Free' and discounts of up to 60 per cent. Officials checked whether the shops were following food safety regulations and took steps to prevent the sale of adulterated, substandard, expired or incorrectly labelled food products, news agency PTI reported.
During inspections at Maxcart Store and Aggarwal Store in Vikaspuri, officials collected five enforcement samples of ghee from different brands and five samples of other food items.
More than 75.50 litres of ghee was seized.

In a separate inspection at Aggarwal Store in Hastal village, the team collected three enforcement samples of ghee sold under the Shri Shan, Vrinda Farms and Avtar brands. Officials seized 246 kg of ghee from the store.
The department said the samples would be assessed alongside laboratory test reports before any further action is taken.

news.exam_corner_topic: Supreme Court expands wetland demarcation mandate, cites drinking water protection
news.headline: Supreme Court expands wetland demarcation mandate, cites drinking water protection
news.story_lead: Supreme Court expands wetland demarcation mandate, cites drinking water protection The court said it cannot remain unmindful of the consequences flowing from water bodies remaining unprotected The Supreme Court has expanded the scope of identification and demarcation of wetlands to all water bodies across the country, observing that courts cannot be unmindful when precious water bodies, being sources of drinking water, remain unprotected. A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi passed the order this month in petitions seeking preservation of wetlands. In December 2024, the court directed states and union territories (UTs) to complete ground truthing and physical demarcation of all wetlands identified in the 2021 Space Applications Centre (SAC) Atlas within three months, as per their statutory obligation under the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017.
news.full_article_text: Supreme Court expands wetland demarcation mandate, cites drinking water protection The court said it cannot remain unmindful of the consequences flowing from water bodies remaining unprotected The Supreme Court has expanded the scope of identification and demarcation of wetlands to all water bodies across the country, observing that courts cannot be unmindful when precious water bodies, being sources of drinking water, remain unprotected. A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi passed the order this month in petitions seeking preservation of wetlands. In December 2024, the court directed states and union territories (UTs) to complete ground truthing and physical demarcation of all wetlands identified in the 2021 Space Applications Centre (SAC) Atlas within three months, as per their statutory obligation under the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017. The court, through subsequent orders over two years, sought responses from states on the extent of work carried out on ground truthing, or physical verification of the wetlands SAC identified under ISRO’s Wetlands Atlas, and physical demarcation of the actual boundaries of these water bodies. The bench called preservation of water bodies, including wetlands, crucial for drinking water needs. “The water bodies being the source of drinking water is precious and would encompass within the four corners of right to live (Article 21), as guaranteed under the Constitution of India,” the bench said in the October 12 order. The petitioners, including birder and environmentalist Anand Arya, informed the bench that the states and UTs have failed to demarcate the wetlands. Several states said that the wetlands identified by the 2021 Wetlands Atlas cannot be traced. In some cases, they said that the wetlands do not need to be protected as they fall outside the definition of wetlands under the 2017 Rules. The bench said the court cannot remain a mere spectator or be unmindful of the consequences flowing from water bodies remaining unprotected as it posted the matter on November 16. “We call upon all the states to file the affidavit indicated hereinabove within an outer limit of four weeks from today indicating the status of ground truthing being done (of wetlands) including other water bodies.” The court described Tamil Nadu as a model state for undertaking the demarcation and ground-truthing exercise in four stages. Tamil Nadu has 28,898 wetlands. The state has so far demarcated 2,614 wetlands and sought six months to identify the remaining ones. As an exception, the court permitted Tamil Nadu to complete the demarcation of all identified wetlands within four months. The court rued that even after nine years from the date of publication of the Rules, ground truthing and demarcation have not been completed or concluded. It directed states and wetland authorities to undertake the exercise as adopted by Tamil Nadu and file a compliance affidavit in four weeks indicating the mode and method of undertaking the exercise. In August 2025, the court noted that the Atlas identified some 555,557 wetlands which are less than 2.25 hectares and asked states to spell out steps being undertaken to protect them. The court, in its October 12 order, reiterated this direction, asking states to identify, specify and mark these wetlands as well.

news.full_article_text: Brics Parliamentary Forum to focus on AI ethics, global challenges: Om Birla Birla said the forum will focus on discussions on global challenges, the proper and human-centric use of AI, parliamentary best practices and capacity building The Brics Parliamentary Forum to be hosted by India next week will discuss pressing global challenges, the ethical use of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies and cooperation for capacity building of lawmakers, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla said on Friday. The meeting, set to be attended by top parliamentary officials from China, Iran and Russia, follows the Brics Summit in September, which concluded with a unanimous joint declaration after the Indian side helped bridge differences between Iran and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) over the West Asia conflict. The Brics Parliamentary Forum, to be held on October 26-27, will have four plenary sessions that will focus on resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability against the backdrop of geopolitical and geo-economic turbulence on the global stage created by conflicts and trade wars. “The forum will focus on discussions on global challenges, the proper and human-centric use of AI and other technologies, parliamentary best practices and capacity building,” Birla told a small group of reporters. He noted that the forum is being held after India successfully hosted the Brics Summit in September. “India has emerged as the voice of the Global South and developing countries. It has taken the lead in getting others to listen to the views of these countries and given priority to their concerns and issues,” he said, noting that trade deals firmed up by the government with several countries have also had a good impact. Besides the main sessions, there will be other sessions that will facilitate interactions between parliamentarians of Brics member states and partners countries, including members of parliamentary foreign affairs committees of several nations. Among those expected to attend the forum are Iran’s Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, a key negotiator for Tehran on issues related to the West Asia conflict and the Strait of Hormuz, the Russian Speaker and a vice chairperson of China’s National People’s Congress. Birla said he will also hold bilateral meetings with the representatives of Brics states and partner countries. These exchanges will facilitate the exchange of ideas on key global challenges and help build bridges between Indian parliamentarians and their counterparts from various countries, he said. The Lok Sabha has also set up parliamentary friendship groups with the parliaments of 64 countries and groupings, such as the European Union, and Baltic and Nordic states. These groups have played a key role in bilateral ties, including when India sent groups of parliamentarians around the world last year to explain its reasons for conducting Operation Sindoor, Birla said. “Such groups play a crucial role in highlighting the changes in India and in influencing opinion about India around the world,” Birla said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Rezaul H Laskar Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015. He began as a journalist in his hometown of Shillong in northeast India and has worked in newspapers and wire services over the years. He moved to New Delhi in 1997 and initially focused on defence, national security, Jammu and Kashmir and the northeast, while also working of foreign policy and international relations. He has been part of the media delegation accompanying PMs on foreign visits and has reported from destinations ranging from Tibet to Ukraine. Between 2007 and 2013, he was the Press Trust of India correspondent in Pakistan, one of only two Indian journalists allowed to report from the country. He extensively covered Pakistan’s domestic politics and the life of the common people, as well as the fallout of the 2008 Mumbai attacks on India-Pakistan relations and the subsequent trial in Pakistan of the suspects involved in the attack. As part of his reportage in Pakistan, he travelled the breadth of the country, from the Swat Valley to Balochistan. Reza’s first gig in journalism was writing a weekly music column, and music – especially classic rock – remains a keen interest. He is also a movie buff and a keen photographer. bullet_points: Brics Parliamentary Forum to focus on AI ethics, global challenges: Om Birla
Birla said the forum will focus on discussions on global challenges, the proper and human-centric use of AI, parliamentary best practices and capacity building

The Brics Parliamentary Forum to be hosted by India next week will discuss pressing global challenges, the ethical use of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies and cooperation for capacity building of lawmakers, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla said on Friday.

The meeting, set to be attended by top parliamentary officials from China, Iran and Russia, follows the Brics Summit in September, which concluded with a unanimous joint declaration after the Indian side helped bridge differences between Iran and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) over the West Asia conflict.

The Brics Parliamentary Forum, to be held on October 26-27, will have four plenary sessions that will focus on resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability against the backdrop of geopolitical and geo-economic turbulence on the global stage created by conflicts and trade wars.

“The forum will focus on discussions on global challenges, the proper and human-centric use of AI and other technologies, parliamentary best practices and capacity building,” Birla told a small group of reporters. He noted that the forum is being held after India successfully hosted the Brics Summit in September.

“India has emerged as the voice of the Global South and developing countries. It has taken the lead in getting others to listen to the views of these countries and given priority to their concerns and issues,” he said, noting that trade deals firmed up by the government with several countries have also had a good impact.

Besides the main sessions, there will be other sessions that will facilitate interactions between parliamentarians of Brics member states and partners countries, including members of parliamentary foreign affairs committees of several nations.

* **मुख्य ध्यान केंद्र:** अंतरिक्ष विज्ञान की प्रगति, तकनीकी ढांचे और आगामी अंतरिक्ष पहलों के लिए संस्थागत समन्वय पर चर्चा।

Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal delivered an impressive performance at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya, Japan, securing a total of three bronze medals. The swimmer, who gained national attention after qualifying for the Paris Paralympics, demonstrated consistent athletic capability across his aquatic events.

- **Achievement**: Medal hat-trick (3 Bronze Medals)

hindi_translation.story_lead: भारतीय पैरा-तैराक हिमांशु नांदल ने जापान के नागोया में आयोजित एशियाई पैरा खेलों में तीन कांस्य पदक जीतकर एक महत्वपूर्ण उपलब्धि हासिल की। पेरिस पैरालिंपिक के लिए क्वालीफाई कर चुके नांदल के प्रदर्शन ने अंतरराष्ट्रीय पैरा-खेलों में भारत की बढ़ती ताकत को रेखांकित किया।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### एशियाई पैरा खेलों में हिमांशु नांदल का प्रदर्शन

भारतीय पैरा-तैराक हिमांशु नांदल ने जापान के नागोया में आयोजित एशियाई पैरा खेलों में कुल तीन कांस्य पदक जीतकर शानदार प्रदर्शन किया। पेरिस पैरालिंपिक के लिए क्वालीफाई करने के बाद राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर ध्यान आकर्षित करने वाले इस तैराक ने अपनी तैराकी स्पर्धाओं में निरंतर क्षमता का प्रदर्शन किया।

### मुख्य बिंदु
- **खिलाड़ी**: हिमांशु नांदल

news.exam_corner_topic: She made India fall in love with women's cricket - now her era as captain is over
news.headline: She made India fall in love with women's cricket - now her era as captain is over
news.story_lead: Harmanpreet Kaur is stepping down as the captain of the India women's cricket team - Published 8 October 2026 When Harmanpreet Kaur scored that unforgettable World Cup century against Australia in the 2017 semi-final, she not only changed the course of a match but the trajectory of women's cricket in India. India went on to lose the final to England that year but women's cricket no longer remained a passing pursuit for the average Indian fan. That dogged zeal to win she infused into the team helped them lift India's first women's World Cup trophy - the same feat that had eluded them in 2017 - in emphatic fashion eight years later.
news.full_article_text: Harmanpreet Kaur is stepping down as the captain of the India women's cricket team - Published 8 October 2026 When Harmanpreet Kaur scored that unforgettable World Cup century against Australia in the 2017 semi-final, she not only changed the course of a match but the trajectory of women's cricket in India. India went on to lose the final to England that year but women's cricket no longer remained a passing pursuit for the average Indian fan. That dogged zeal to win she infused into the team helped them lift India's first women's World Cup trophy - the same feat that had eluded them in 2017 - in emphatic fashion eight years later. Less than a year on, and within weeks of victories in the Asia Cup and the Asian Games, she has relinquished the captaincy, ending an era in which she became the team's most influential leader and one of the most recognisable figures in the sport. Star opener Smriti Mandhana, her long-time deputy, has been appointed captain across all formats. Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) secretary Devajit Saikia, coach Amol Muzumdar, Harmanpreet and Mandhana attended the review meeting at which the leadership change was ratified. The transition, however, was not entirely seamless. Reports suggest the 37-year-old Harmanpreet was willing to relinquish the T20 captaincy immediately, but was keen to continue leading the side in One-Day Internationals and Tests so that younger players could benefit from her experience. The BCCI, however, was intent on a younger person at the helm and opted for the 30-year-old Mandhana. In some ways, the move mirrors the BCCI's decision to replace Suryakumar Yadav as captain of the men's T20 side shortly after India won the World Cup earlier this year, with the captaincy passing to Shreyas Iyer. Harmanpreet's future as captain had become a subject of intense debate in cricketing circles after India's below-par performance at the T20 World Cup in England a few months ago. Her own poor form with the bat amplified concerns and prompted the BCCI to consider changes that could help the team meet the growing challenges of a women's game that continues to expand rapidly around the world. Approaching her 38th birthday, and after almost a decade at the helm, Harmanpreet found herself under increasing scrutiny as her form dipped. Harmanpreet led the India women's team to a famous World Cup win in 2025 Opinion on whether she should continue as captain was sharply divided among former women players and captains. Former cricketer Diana Edulji, among the most respected names in the game, felt Harmanpreet had done everything that could reasonably have been expected of her and that it was time for a younger captain to take over. Former captain Anjum Chopra, meanwhile, argued that Harmanpreet's experience remained invaluable and that she should stay on. Sensing that the BCCI was strongly inclined towards a change, Harmanpreet opted to step down during the review meeting. She later announced her decision in an emotional Instagram post. "I feel I have done my duty. I gave this team everything I had," she wrote. "Now, it is time for me to turn the pageâ¦ Blood. Sweat. Sacrifice. Pride. I gave it all. Now, I'm ready to play for the love of the game again. "Captaincy ends, the journey continues." Harmanpreet's intention to continue playing now leaves the BCCI with another decision to make about her future. In Suryakumar Yadav's case, he not only lost the captaincy but also his place in India's T20 side. Given the depth of talent available in the men's game, it was easier for Ajit Agarkar and his fellow selectors to take what was always likely to be a contentious decision. The situation in the women's game is different. Despite Harmanpreet's modest recent form, replacing a player of her experience and stature may not be straightforward, as the talent pipeline is not yet as deep as it is in men's cricket. Whatever the future holds, Harmanpreet has scripted among the more memorable careers in women's cricket. Spanning more than two decades, it is a journey marked by significant achievements and milestones. Harmanpreet (left) has now passed the captaincy baton to Smriti Mandhana (right) Born into a family of modest means in Punjab's Moga city, Harmanpreet developed a passion for cricket at an early age. Her family's support was vital in the early years, but her rise to national recognition came after she joined the Railways - a transition facilitated by Diana Edulji - and moved to Mumbai. The superior facilities and greater professionalism associated with Mumbai's sporting culture helped accelerate her development. She made her India debut in 2009 at the age of 20 and has remained an integral part of the national side across formats ever since. An all-rounder for the better part of her first decade in cricket, she made herself indispensable to the side with her explosive middle-order batting, crafty off-spin and sharp fielding skills. Her blistering century against Australia in the semi-final of the 2017 Women's ODI World Cup remains one of the defining knocks in the history of the women's game. India went on to lose to England in the final, but beating Australia was a monumental hurdle overcome. That century also helped spark wider interest in women's cricket in India, and transformed Harmanpreet into a household name. Harmanpreet made her debut in the India women's cricket team in 2009 The second decade of her career showcased her prowess both as batter and captain. Having succeeded Mithali Raj as T20 captain in 2016, Harmanpreet assumed charge across all formats in 2022 and went on to guide India to some of the greatest successes in its history. Her leadership was marked by an aggressive pursuit of victory. That fearless approach instilled confidence and ambition in her teammates, helping the team overcome even the previously unbeatable Australians, most memorably in the semi-final of the 2025 ODI World Cup. Unlike in 2017, Harmanpreet couldn't get a hundred on that occasion, but her innings of 89 was a stellar effort as captain. Combined with Jemimah Rodrigues's century, it helped India secure a famous victory over their arch rivals. India then defeated South Africa in the final to reach what many regard as the pinnacle of achievement in the history of Indian women's cricket. With multiple titles and trophies won under her leadership, Harmanpreet leaves behind a formidable legacy for her successor, Smriti Mandhana, to emulate. Related topics

news.headline: Karnataka asks hospitals to reveal medicine purchase prices, display procedure costs
news.story_lead: Karnataka asks hospitals to reveal medicine purchase prices, display procedure costs The measures are intended to give patients a clearer account of medicine costs and bring greater transparency to hospital billing. From November 1, patients at hospitals across Karnataka will be able to see what hospitals paid for medicines as well as their maximum retail prices, under new billing requirements announced by the state government. Karnataka health and family welfare minister U T Khader said in Bengaluru that hospitals in the state will have to record both figures on patient bills and use the disclosed prices while charging for medicines.
news.full_article_text: Karnataka asks hospitals to reveal medicine purchase prices, display procedure costs The measures are intended to give patients a clearer account of medicine costs and bring greater transparency to hospital billing. From November 1, patients at hospitals across Karnataka will be able to see what hospitals paid for medicines as well as their maximum retail prices, under new billing requirements announced by the state government. Karnataka health and family welfare minister U T Khader said in Bengaluru that hospitals in the state will have to record both figures on patient bills and use the disclosed prices while charging for medicines. Medicine price lists will also have to be displayed in prominent public areas, particularly near registration counters. The government is also considering greater disclosure of procedure costs. Hospitals could display prices for major medical procedures on notice boards, while charges for other procedures could be maintained in a ledger that patients could consult when required, Khader said. The proposed rules will not require private hospitals to adopt the rates charged at government facilities. Instead, Khader said private hospital charges could vary depending on the amenities and level of treatment provided. “We are not expecting the pricing at private hospitals to be on par with the price set at government hospitals, but the rates could be fixed based on the amenities provided and the level of treatment at the hospital,” he said. The government’s proposed changes will therefore cover not only the disclosure of medicine purchase prices and MRPs on bills, but also the public display of medicine prices and, potentially, procedure charges. No punishment for violation yet The state has yet to decide what action hospitals could face for failing to comply with the new requirements. The Health Department plans to meet private hospitals shortly to discuss and finalise the terms and conditions. “The punishment for violating the rules would be discussed,” U T Khader said. He said the government did not want regulations to make healthcare businesses financially unviable, while arguing that tighter rules were necessary. “We do not intend to push the healthcare business into loss, but some stringent rules and regulations will have to be put in place,” he said. Minister blames foreign investment for rising healthcare costs Khader said the government was concerned about the rise in healthcare costs and, in his view, linked part of the increase to the entry of foreign investors into the healthcare sector. “According to my observation, after foreign investors have entered the healthcare market, the prices have gone up tremendously. We will discuss and see what best can be done,” he said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Arun Dev Arun Dev is an Assistant Editor with the Karnataka bureau of Hindustan Times. A journalist for over 10 years, he has written extensively on crime and politics.
