news.headline: No dilution in prescribed standards: NMC on denotification of medical education regulations
news.story_lead: No dilution in prescribed standards: NMC on denotification of medical education regulations New Delhi, The National Medical Commission has asserted that the de-notification of the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 will not dilute prescribed standards of medical education and are intended to remove overlapping procedures. The Commission, which is the statutory body for medical education in the country, had on October 14 denotified the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations . The denotification "does not, in any manner, dilute the prescribed standards of medical education or the regulatory oversight exercised by NMC," a statement by the Commission said.
news.full_article_text: No dilution in prescribed standards: NMC on denotification of medical education regulations New Delhi, The National Medical Commission has asserted that the de-notification of the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 will not dilute prescribed standards of medical education and are intended to remove overlapping procedures. The Commission, which is the statutory body for medical education in the country, had on October 14 denotified the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations . The denotification "does not, in any manner, dilute the prescribed standards of medical education or the regulatory oversight exercised by NMC," a statement by the Commission said. Under the National Medical Commission Act, 2019, the Undergraduate Medical Education Board and Postgraduate Medical Education Board are primarily entrusted with prescribing academic standards, minimum requirements and educational norms. The Medical Assessment and Rating Board , under Section 26 of the Act is specifically empowered to assess and inspect medical institutions, verify compliance with prescribed standards and initiate appropriate regulatory measures against institutions found deficient, it stated. The regulations had introduced a parallel mechanism of institutional evaluation, annual renewal and enforcement through UGMEB and PGMEB, resulting in overlapping regulatory functions, the statement. Following judicial observations and a detailed examination of the statutory framework, the Commission decided to remove this duplication and align regulatory responsibilities with the provisions of the NMC Act, it stated. The requirement of Annual Disclosure Reports remains mandatory and medical colleges will continue to submit annual disclosures concerning faculty, infrastructure, clinical facilities, patient load and other prescribed parameters, it emphasised. These disclosures remain available for scrutiny and verification through the statutory assessment and inspection mechanisms of MARB. Therefore, any suggestion that annual disclosures would become merely unverified claims is misplaced, the statement said. Further, all existing minimum standard requirements relating to faculty, infrastructure, clinical material, teaching facilities, attendance and academic standards will remain fully applicable. The MARB retains its statutory authority to conduct assessments and inspections, including where necessary without prior notice, and to take appropriate action against non-compliant institutions under the NMC Act and Regulation of the Establishment of Medical Institutions, Assessment and Rating Regulations, 2023, the statement said. The de-notification also safeguards actions already taken, liabilities incurred and proceedings initiated under MSMER-2023. The decision neither provides immunity for past violations nor exempts medical colleges from future regulatory action, it stressed. The only procedural change is the removal of the additional annual renewal requirement under MSMER-2023. Medical colleges remain subject to mandatory annual disclosures, prescribed minimum standards, institutional assessment and statutory enforcement. "NMC remains committed to maintaining the highest standards of medical education while ensuring that regulation is transparent, effective and free from unnecessary duplication. Regulatory simplification must not be mistaken for regulatory relaxation," it stated. "The NMC has removed an overlapping process, not the safeguards that protect the quality of medical education," the statement added. Speaking at a roundtable during the Berlin Global Dialogue, Goyal said Western countries were largely responsible for the environmental damage caused by ozone layer depletion and carbon emissions. He also told the roundtable that India's contribution to global carbon emissions was only three to four percentage points lower than Europe's, despite India having a population of 1.4 billion and accounting for 17 per cent of the world's population. Goyal said India's per capita carbon emissions remain significantly lower than those of Western countries, arguing that Europe’s per capita emissions and environmental impact are seven to eight times higher than India's. “Even today, as we sit here, my per capita contribution to carbon emissions is probably less than 10 per cent or 15 per cent of yours. Even today, Europe's per capita contribution to carbon emissions—and its per capita environmental impact—is probably seven or eight times that of India,” Goyal said. Also Read | If current policies continue, warming could reach 2.8°C within this century: UN report What happened to $100 billion climate finance pledge, Goyal questions? Goyal also reminded the developed countries of the world about the pledge to provide financial and technological support to developing and vulnerable nations under the Paris Agreement. He said that as per the agreement, developed countries were to assist developing countries with climate finance worth $100 billion but not a ‘dime of it’ has been received. "At the Paris climate conference in 2015, when the whole world came together, it was Prime Minister Modi who brought the Global South together and encouraged countries to commit to addressing climate change at COP21. It was agreed that the developed countries, who have enjoyed the fruits of messing up the climate for so many decades, will pay a greater price, and will support the developing and less developed countries, as well as island nations in the Pacific and the Caribbean...Just $100 billion a year. That was the commitment," Goyal said. Also Read | Ahead of COP31 next month, what has India committed to and what does it expect? “Eleven years later, we haven't seen a nickel or a dime of that. It's all promises. The larger question that the European Union and CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) have failed to answer,” Goyal added. India reportedly recorded a decline in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in 2025 compared to the previous year, breaking a prolonged trend of rapid growth, according to the United Nations Environment Programme's (UNEP) annual Emissions Gap Report released on Wednesday. The decline was attributed partly to weather-related factors and partly to structural shifts towards renewable energy. bullet_points: ‘You are responsible for this mess’: Piyush Goyal slams West over carbon emissions, climate finance failures
Goyal reminded the developed countries of the pledge to provide financial and technological support to developing nations under the Paris Agreement

Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal blamed developed countries for contributing a disproportionately large share of global carbon emissions while failing to honour the climate finance commitments they made at COP21 in Paris in 2015.

Speaking at a roundtable during the Berlin Global Dialogue, Goyal said Western countries were largely responsible for the environmental damage caused by ozone layer depletion and carbon emissions. He also told the roundtable that India's contribution to global carbon emissions was only three to four percentage points lower than Europe's, despite India having a population of 1.4 billion and accounting for 17 per cent of the world's population.
Also Read | Emissions didn't spike in 2025. That doesn't mean climate crisis has been stopped in its tracks

"Who's responsible for this mess in the first place? Where did the ozone layer get damaged? Who sent all that carbon into the atmosphere? I represent 17% of the world's population, but my contribution to global carbon emissions is less than 3%. You (Europe) represent probably 3% or 4% of the world's population, yet your contribution to those carbon emissions—or this mess—is humongous. The problem was caused by you," Goyal said.

Goyal said India's per capita carbon emissions remain significantly lower than those of Western countries, arguing that Europe’s per capita emissions and environmental impact are seven to eight times higher than India's.

“Even today, as we sit here, my per capita contribution to carbon emissions is probably less than 10 per cent or 15 per cent of yours. Even today, Europe's per capita contribution to carbon emissions—and its per capita environmental impact—is probably seven or eight times that of India,” Goyal said.

news.headline: India-US trade deal in ‘last stage’, says EAM Jaishankar: ‘It’s never done until it’s done’
news.story_lead: India-US trade deal in ‘last stage’, says EAM Jaishankar: ‘It’s never done until it’s done’ The trade deal figured in Jaishankar’s meeting with Rubio this week after the secretary of state visited India for the second time in less than five months. The India-US trade agreement is in its “last mile” but “it’s never done till it’s done”, external affairs minister S Jaishankar said on Thursday about efforts by the two countries to find common ground on the deal they have negotiated for more than a year. US secretary of state Marco Rubio and commerce minister Piyush Goyal too have spoken of the two sides moving towards the final stages of the trade deal, he said at a session at the NDTV World Summit.
news.full_article_text: India-US trade deal in ‘last stage’, says EAM Jaishankar: ‘It’s never done until it’s done’ The trade deal figured in Jaishankar’s meeting with Rubio this week after the secretary of state visited India for the second time in less than five months. The India-US trade agreement is in its “last mile” but “it’s never done till it’s done”, external affairs minister S Jaishankar said on Thursday about efforts by the two countries to find common ground on the deal they have negotiated for more than a year. US secretary of state Marco Rubio and commerce minister Piyush Goyal too have spoken of the two sides moving towards the final stages of the trade deal, he said at a session at the NDTV World Summit. “But…often the last mile or the penultimate miles do pose their challenges. I think the [negotiating] teams are working through them now,” Jaishankar said. “If you’re asking me to tell you what exactly those challenges are, I’m sorry I won’t. That’s for the negotiators to sort out.” Also Read I US ‘very close’ to India trade deal; energy needs considered in Russia sanctions waiver: Marco Rubio S Jaishankar addresses India-US ties The trade deal figured in Jaishankar’s meeting with Rubio in Mumbai this week after the secretary of state visited India for the second time in less than five months. Bilateral ties have been hit by the Trump administration’s unpredictable trade policies, immigration restrictions that have impacted Indian professionals and growing ties between Washington and the Pakistani military leadership. Jaishankar said he failed to understand criticism by opposition parties of his visit to Mumbai to meet Rubio, which Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had described as a “summoning”. “They have something against Mumbai. It’s our financial capital, it’s our Bollywood capital. It has got so much going for it. Maybe Mumbai doesn’t like them, I have no idea why they have this reservation,” the minister said. Jaishankar listed examples of Indian leaders travelling out of New Delhi to meet foreign dignitaries, including two instances involving Congress leaders – former PM Indira Gandhi met Pakistani leader Zulfikar Ali Bhutto in Shimla in 1972 to sign the Simla Agreement, and Union minister Salman Khurshid hosted a lunch for then Pakistan PM Raja Pervez Ashraf in Jaipur in 2013. “We are adults, let’s have an adult conversation,” he said, taking a swipe at Rahul Gandhi. On Pakistan and terrorism Jaishankar also spoke on the issue of Pakistan-backed terrorism and said India does not want to wait for the US and other countries to understand its concerns on terror. He emphasised that the world takes note only when a country responds to terrorism, and India has done so through Operation Sindoor and the Balakot air strikes. While India desires good relations with Pakistan, it is unwilling to overlook terrorism to achieve this, he said. He responded to a question on Pakistan’s military leadership wooing the Trump administration in the US and the perception that Washington hasn’t fully understood New Delhi’s concerns on cross-border terror by saying the issue is much broader. “If Washington understood it so well, why didn’t we act in 2008, when 26/11 happened? And when we did act, we didn’t act because Washington understood it, we acted because we understood it,” he said. “First of all, forget about somebody else getting terrorism right. Get it right yourself. If you don’t have the clarity of thought, the conviction to fight back against terrorism, don’t think somebody else is going to do that job for you.” Also Read I ‘India diversified imports, but hard to pivot in one day’: Marco Rubio explains why US waived some Russia energy tariffs India’s counter-terror policy has evolved and this was evident in the response to cross-border terror with last year’s Operation Sindoor, the Balakot air strikes in 2019, and the surgical strikes across the Line of Control in 2016. “The evolution is that if terrorism goes on, it will not be business as usual. It is not, you will take a break and then say, ‘Okay, now it has been a long time. Let me get back to talking to them again’, which is what the pattern was,” he said. “The 26/11 attacks should serve as a reminder of the enormity of what is being done to us and the necessity for us to respond. And when you respond, the world will take note. When you don’t respond, the world will play games.” When Jaishankar was asked if India, which has made it clear that terrorism and talks cannot go together, still wishes to have better relations with Pakistan, he said the reality was Islamabad was using terrorism as state policy. “Of course we want good relations with Pakistan, we want that with all our neighbours but will I overlook terror for that? I will not. The government is very clear,” he said. “The national mood on Pakistan changed after 26/11. Till then, there were people who would keep making these arguments. After 26/11, only the government of the day made the argument.” United Nations and protests Jaishankar responded to another question on whether the UN has “double standards” on protests in different countries by saying that the answer is “pretty obvious”. The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights and UN human rights experts have expressed concern over the government’s handling of protests associated with the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and other groups. “That is a bigger issue because you get into what the UN is, what positions they take, and so forth. Let’s be straightforward about it, I am making this assessment and observation about what is happening across multiple countries and societies. This is not a comment specific to India, the Indian subcontinent or France,” Jaishankar said. “We have seen that in many cases, when these moments occur, there is external encouragement and external support. There is a set of actors who see this as a tool of influence to advance their agenda. It is not a secret – even those who do it openly admit to it, they are not hiding it,” he said. Also Read I 'Very close, some items left': Marco Rubio optimistic about India-US trade deal Jaishankar also spoke about his choice of streaming shows based on diplomacy and how closely they reflect realities. He said he watches The Diplomat on Netflix but noted that the series presents diplomacy in a distinctly American way. “I’m watching The Diplomat but I want to say one thing. No value judgement here but The Diplomat is very quintessentially American. Even then, when you make these shows, you make them because you want to dramatise things,” he said. “If I made a real show about how diplomacy works, people would go to sleep.” Jaishankar added, “I look at it with a somewhat critical eye. I relate to some of it. I looked at the ambassador having reflux and told myself, ‘Okay, that problem I know.’ So the point is, I travel, I read, I do everything which you guys do. But it’s always a bit of a busman’s holiday. When you look at some of these thin

news.headline: India, Poland pledge to deepen ties in defence, nuclear energy
news.story_lead: India, Poland pledge to deepen ties in defence, nuclear energy New Delhi India and Poland on Thursday agreed to deepen cooperation in defence, space and nuclear energy as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Polish counterpart Donald Tusk focused on leveraging the economic growth of both countries to achieve the shared target of doubling trade from the current level of $6 billion by 2030 New Delhi India and Poland on Thursday agreed to deepen cooperation in defence, space and nuclear energy as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Polish counterpart Donald Tusk focused on leveraging the economic growth of both countries to achieve the shared target of doubling trade from the current level of $6 billion by 2030. news.full_article_text: India, Poland pledge to deepen ties in defence, nuclear energy New Delhi India and Poland on Thursday agreed to deepen cooperation in defence, space and nuclear energy as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Polish counterpart Donald Tusk focused on leveraging the economic growth of both countries to achieve the shared target of doubling trade from the current level of $6 billion by 2030 New Delhi India and Poland on Thursday agreed to deepen cooperation in defence, space and nuclear energy as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Polish counterpart Donald Tusk focused on leveraging the economic growth of both countries to achieve the shared target of doubling trade from the current level of $6 billion by 2030. Bilateral ties got a major boost with Modi’s visit to Warsaw in 2024, the first by an Indian PM in 45 years, and defence and security have emerged as a key area for cooperation as Poland is currently engaged in the largest military modernisation campaign in Europe by spending almost 5% of its GDP on its armed forces against the backdrop of the war in Ukraine. Modi described his discussions with Tusk as “excellent” and said on social media the two leaders discussed bolstering cooperation in trade, investment, defence, nuclear energy, space and critical minerals. Regional and global issues also figured in the talks, and Indian officials said the Polish side appreciated India’s recent proposal for a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire. “Today, we agreed to deepen our cooperation in defence, space and nuclear energy. In all these strategic sectors, we invite Polish companies to partner with India in co-development and co-production,” Modi said at a media interaction with Tusk. Tusk added, “We are very aware of political threats and the need to become independent as much as possible in the area of…minerals and strategic resources…to make sure that Poland and India are independent in those areas.” India and Poland, Modi said, have emerged as centres of growth and technology at a time of uncertainty and change. “Last year, Poland’s GDP crossed the historic milestone of $1 trillion…Meanwhile, India recorded an impressive growth rate of 7.8% in the last quarter,” he said, noting that the proposed India-European Union (EU) trade deal will open new opportunities for India to export machinery, chemicals, plastics and engineering goods to Poland. “At the same time, we will seek new investments from Poland in sectors such as railways and mobility, advanced manufacturing, food processing and biotechnology,” Modi said, adding that Tusk is accompanied by a large business delegation that will focus on developing trusted supply chains to achieve the shared goal of doubling trade by 2030. The two sides will also develop new partnerships in critical minerals and coal gasification using Polish expertise, and establish a bilateral “startup bridge” to build on cooperation in AI, cybersecurity and fintech, Modi said. The business delegation of almost 100 Polish companies will participate in two business forums in New Delhi and Bengaluru to explore collaboration in defence, agri-tech, food processing, pharmaceuticals, mining, technology and infrastructure. Two-way trade is currently worth $6.3 billion, and Indian investments in Poland have grown to $3 billion, with Indian IT companies having a significant presence. Tusk noted the two countries were able to build synergy as they have no conflicts of interest or historical issues that divide them. He also lauded Modi’s role on the global stage, describing it as a “beacon of hope” at a time of destabilisation and political uncertainty. He pointed to growing defence cooperation between the two sides and said: “Our drones were very useful…recently and I am convinced that cooperation in satellites and drones has helped our countries in times of political tensions and crises.” Tusk’s comments were an apparent reference to the use of Polish loitering munitions or drones by India’s military against Pakistan during Operation Sindoor, last year’s campaign that targeted terrorist infrastructure on Pakistani soil in retaliation for the Pahalgam attack. Poland’s WB Group supplied 100 units of Warmate loitering munitions to the Indian Army in 2022, and Polish officials said earlier this year that the army had signed three more defence contracts. Poland is also eyeing tie-ups with Indian manufacturers of munitions to replenish ammunition stocks depleted by supplies provided to Ukraine since the start of the Russian invasion in 2022. However, some Polish firms have concerns about India’s long-standing military ties with Russia, and New Delhi and Warsaw are finalising an agreement on secure information exchanges to boost defence industrial cooperation. Sibi George, secretary (West) in the external affairs ministry, told a media briefing the two sides are working on an agreement on mutual protection and exchange of classified information that is expected to build on the growing trust between India and the EU in areas such as defence and technology. With both countries eyeing joint development and production of military gear, it is important to have agreements to put in place trust and confidentiality, he said. The two sides also agreed to establish a defence industry dialogue and a counter-terrorism dialogue, George said. The security and defence partnership concluded by India and the EU earlier this year provides an additional framework for strategic cooperation with Poland in defence, counter-terrorism, technology, cybersecurity, space and shipbuilding, he said. Modi also referred to his discussions with Tusk on regional and global issues and said: “Whether in Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort towards peace.” George said Poland was “very appreciative” of India’s approach for a diplomatic solution to the Russia-Ukraine conflict, and Modi’s recent call to Russian President Vladimir Putin to move from “endless war to the end of war”. news.exam_corner_topic: Telangana to host first state-organised defence and aerospace expo, curtain-raiser on Saturday
news.headline: Telangana to host first state-organised defence and aerospace expo, curtain-raiser on Saturday
news.story_lead: Telangana to host first state-organised defence and aerospace expo, curtain-raiser on Saturday The main event, scheduled from December 7 to 9 will bring together the aerospace, space, defence, and internal security sectors on a single platform. Telangana is set to host Raksha Expo 2026—India’s first defence and aerospace expo organised by a state government—with the curtain-raiser scheduled to be held in Hyderabad on October 24. The main event, scheduled from December 7 to 9 at Bharat Future City, will bring together the aerospace, space, defence, and internal security sectors on a single platform to promote domestic manufacturing, innovation, and investment.
news.full_article_text: Telangana to host first state-organised defence and aerospace expo, curtain-raiser on Saturday The main event, scheduled from December 7 to 9 will bring together the aerospace, space, defence, and internal security sectors on a single platform. Telangana is set to host Raksha Expo 2026—India’s first defence and aerospace expo organised by a state government—with the curtain-raiser scheduled to be held in Hyderabad on October 24. The main event, scheduled from December 7 to 9 at Bharat Future City, will bring together the aerospace, space, defence, and internal security sectors on a single platform to promote domestic manufacturing, innovation, and investment. “The nature of conflict is changing. Conventional methods of warfare and statecraft now operate alongside drones and new-age missiles. Telangana must be the centre of this revolution. We must be the largest contributors to India’s national and internal security,” Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy said. “Telangana must become the largest contributor to the mission of securing India’s national and internal security. I am confident Telangana will help make India a global defence superpower,” he said. The program The curtain-raiser is expected to bring together more than 80 leaders from over 70 organisations, including global original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and Indian defence and aerospace companies. Companies represented include Airbus, Boeing, Tata Lockheed Martin, Safran, Rolls-Royce and GE Aerospace, among others. Union defence minister Rajnath Singh has been invited to inaugurate the main expo. The state government has also planned a roadshow in New Delhi on October 29 to build participation ahead of the December summit. The expo will be held as a flagship event alongside the Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026. Its programme will include exhibitions, live technology demonstrations, drone shows and a planned air show on December 9. Business-to-business and business-to-government meetings are expected to connect manufacturers, startups, and micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with government representatives, security agencies, and international investors. The aim is to enable supplier partnerships, joint ventures, technology transfer, and indigenous co-development. Hyderabad’s existing aerospace and defence ecosystem will be central to the showcase. The city is home to more than 12 Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) laboratories and defence public sector enterprises, as well as private manufacturers such as Tata Advanced Systems, Adani Defence and Bharat Forge. The Telangana Rising 2047 link The state’s aerospace network has produced 400 Apache helicopter fuselages. It also serves as the global single source for C-130J Super Hercules empennages— the structure at the rear of an aircraft responsible for aerodynamic stability. The event is also linked to the state’s Telangana Rising 2047 vision, which seeks to position Telangana as a major economic and manufacturing hub and achieve the status of a $1 trillion economy by 2034. “Hyderabad has powered India’s strategic programmes for decades, from missiles and fighter aircraft to satellites and secure communications, and is home to nearly 30 per cent of the country’s defence and aerospace industry,” said chief secretary Sanjay Jaju. The event comes amid a push to strengthen domestic defence manufacturing and reduce vulnerabilities in global supply chains. India’s defence production reached a record ₹ 1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26, while defence exports touched ₹ 38,424 crore. Telangana’s aerospace exports also rose from ₹ 15,900 crore in 2023-24 to ₹ 30,742 crore in 2024-25.

news.story_lead: Ex-US and French ambassadors Lynne Tracy and Pierre LÃ©vy were among those to speak to the BBC of their time in Moscow - Published 5 hours ago "Being the ambassador to Russia was probably the hardest assignment of my career," Lynne Tracy, who represented the US in Moscow from 2023 and 2025, tells the BBC. US, UK and European diplomats once played a crucial role in Russia, defusing tensions even at the worst moments of the Cold War. But now, deemed "unfriendly" by President Vladimir Putin's government, Western ambassadors are under constant surveillance, isolated and increasingly cut off from the country they were sent to understand, as the war in Ukraine grinds on through its fifth year.
news.full_article_text: Ex-US and French ambassadors Lynne Tracy and Pierre LÃ©vy were among those to speak to the BBC of their time in Moscow - Published 5 hours ago "Being the ambassador to Russia was probably the hardest assignment of my career," Lynne Tracy, who represented the US in Moscow from 2023 and 2025, tells the BBC. US, UK and European diplomats once played a crucial role in Russia, defusing tensions even at the worst moments of the Cold War. But now, deemed "unfriendly" by President Vladimir Putin's government, Western ambassadors are under constant surveillance, isolated and increasingly cut off from the country they were sent to understand, as the war in Ukraine grinds on through its fifth year. The BBC has spoken to five diplomats who have served in Russia since it launched its full-scale invasion. They compare current pressure levels to the Cold War era - when Western embassies were monitored through physical surveillance, listening devices hidden inside gifts , and "spy dust" - a near invisible chemical agent used to track officials. Hundreds of Russian diplomats were expelled from countries in Europe and the US after the war began in 2022. Moscow responded in kind, declaring hundreds of Western diplomats persona non grata and leaving many embassies short-staffed. Tracy's 30-year career took her to countries like Pakistan, where she survived an armed attack in 2008. But she says that even under constant physical threat, her posting in Peshawar was, in a sense, easier than Russia. "There, I still felt that there were things within my control. What made Moscow more difficult were the high levels of uncertainty." The constant pressure from Russian counterintelligence was the primary source of such uncertainty, she recalls. Tracy pictured leaving Russia's Foreign Ministry after being summoned by Moscow in 2023 Russian diplomats in the West also complain of such unfair treatment. But according to the diplomats who spoke to the BBC, the scope and tactics of Moscow's intelligence services are far greater. "Expect listening devices, expect cameras in every single room of your house," a former European diplomat says of the warning he received before leaving for Moscow. Another ex-ambassador says they were forced to dismiss two Russian employees after Moscow's domestic security service, the FSB, tried to recruit them, demanding that they report on everything going on at the diplomatic mission. The pair told the embassy instead, who let them go - "otherwise, they could have faced some sort of criminal prosecution". Meanwhile, Russians who would ordinarily build relationships with diplomatic staff - such as those working in academia and culture - are also being intimidated into avoiding contact with Western officials. One former ambassador says his guests were once "tailed" by FSB agents right up to the doors of the embassy. - Inside the shadowy world of anti-Putin sabotage from within Russia Published 4 days ago - Europe targeted by spiralling campaign of sabotage - and Russia is the chief suspect Published 4 September - They fled Russia, but the West sent them back Published 7 days ago Just this June, guests invited to the British ambassador's residence in Moscow for the King's birthday celebrations said they had been harassed by pro-Kremlin activists and state-media journalists, and then questioned by the police. One of the guests says he has since declined several invitations to events at Western embassies out of fear. Not everyone can deal with the pressure. One former ambassador says "constant paranoia" has driven a number of officials to quit their jobs. Even after leaving Russia himself, he adds, he was looking over his shoulder for months. 'Generals prove what they can do in war. The same is true for diplomats' In the immediate aftermath of the invasion, there were discussions across Europe about whether to recall ambassadors or stop working in Russia altogether, says former French ambassador Pierre LÃ©vy. He remembers calling Paris immediately to say pulling their envoys would be a mistake, feeling that the worse relations became, the more important they would be. The invasion quickly transformed their work, says another ex-European ambassador; the co-operation required for their usual efforts on bilateral relations, trade and joint projects was now impossible. And for those who stayed in Russia, the war left them with a host of new priorities beyond supporting their own citizens and companies. Firstly, countries viewed as unfriendly by Moscow still wanted at least some channel of communication with Russian officials to get an accurate picture of what was happening inside the country. But they also had to protect their staff and keep their embassies functioning. Pierre LÃ©vy (second from the left) and Lynne Tracy (second from the right) pictured at the funeral service for opposition leader Alexei Navalny in March 2024 After Russia's ban on hiring foreign nationals in 2021, the US embassy's facilities team was left significantly understaffed. Ðven a minor plumbing issue like a leaking pipe could turn into a major problem, draining the time of diplomatic workers. One diplomat recalls discussing staffing shortages with a Russian official, who advised him not to get too upset. "He said, 'at least you still have the chef'." Financial sanctions imposed by Western governments to support Ukraine created different day-to-day difficulties. After Russian banks were cut off from the Swift payment network, and Mastercard and Visa suspended operations in Russia, many embassies struggled with basic operating expenses. A former ambassador recalls simply running out of cash and being unable to pay his staff - until another diplomat, who was selling his car after being expelled, brought the rubles to the embassy in a suitcase. "It's completely insane," the diplomat laughs. "But you had to look at it with a sense of humour." A wooden replica of the Great Seal of the US was given to the American ambassador to Russia as a gift in 1945 - it was later found to contain a listening device Russian officials make little secret of their attitude towards Western diplomats. They have openly accused those from "unfriendly countries" of engaging in "espionage". Moscow has been particularly critical of those who show an interest in expressions of dissent against the Kremlin and, according to Russian journalist Alexei Venediktov, has effectively banned most Russian officials from speaking to Western embassies. This has only worsened relations with the West, says Venediktov, who recalls telling Russian officials: "You are being misunderstood precisely because of your own actions - because ambassadors cannot do their jobs." Today, Moscow has little to no contact with many Western governments, says one ex-European ambassador. "There are no calls, no meetings at ministerial level." news.exam_corner_topic: In a first, UN's Loss and Damage Fund sets aside $21.6 million for Nepal for Bhote Koshi disaster
news.headline: In a first, UN's Loss and Damage Fund sets aside $21.6 million for Nepal for Bhote Koshi disaster
news.story_lead: In a first, UN's Loss and Damage Fund sets aside $21.6 million for Nepal for Bhote Koshi disaster It is the first time money has been allocated to or set aside for a country since the fund's creation and marks a pivotal point. For the first time since it was operationalised at COP 28, the United Nations’ (UN) Loss and Damage Fund has provisionally approved $20 million plus $1.6 million in oversight fees for Nepal on Thursday for the damage caused during August’s Bhote Koshi River floods, which killed at least 1,000 people and left over 5,000 missing. The Board for the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) met at an “extraordinary meeting” on Thursday to address a formal climate-emergency funding request from Nepal for $20 million over a four-year period.
news.full_article_text: In a first, UN's Loss and Damage Fund sets aside $21.6 million for Nepal for Bhote Koshi disaster It is the first time money has been allocated to or set aside for a country since the fund's creation and marks a pivotal point. For the first time since it was operationalised at COP 28, the United Nations’ (UN) Loss and Damage Fund has provisionally approved $20 million plus $1.6 million in oversight fees for Nepal on Thursday for the damage caused during August’s Bhote Koshi River floods, which killed at least 1,000 people and left over 5,000 missing. The Board for the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) met at an “extraordinary meeting” on Thursday to address a formal climate-emergency funding request from Nepal for $20 million over a four-year period. This accounts for only around 0.7% of the costs estimated to be incurred by Nepal during the disaster. However, it is the first time money has been allocated to or set aside for a country since the fund's creation and marks a pivotal point in developing countries' efforts to access climate finance for disasters. The Loss and Damage Fund was set up to provide financial assistance to developing countries that are especially vulnerable to the adverse effects of climate change – helping them cope with unavoidable economic and non-economic losses Experts said Nepal will still have to formally apply for this funding, and the Board will consider the request at its next meeting in December. This is the maximum amount that can currently be requested for a single project. The funding is expected to cover about 0.7% of the costs of the August Nepal floods, which preliminary estimates suggest could be around US$2.56 billion. The co-chairs received a communication from the Government of Nepal via its senior signatory national focal point on August 31. Within the communication, Nepal requested that the Board “take a special decision to respond rapidly, directly and effectively in accordance with its Governing Instrument”. Applications and contributions So far, developing countries have submitted 176 applications to the fund, totalling $2.8 billion, a separate analysis by Carbon Brief shows. As of March 15 this year, the Loss and Damage Fund had received $822.06 million in pledges from 27 countries, with total grant contributions currently standing at $ 629.70 million. The largest contributors include the UAE ($100 million); Germany ($98.4 million); France ($ 53.07 million); the United Kingdom ($ 52.15 million); Spain ($ 44.01 million); and Australia ($ 34.11 million). Harjeet Singh, Global Convenor, Fill the Fund campaign and Founding Director, Satat Sampada Climate Foundation, said Thursday marked a historic day in responding to Nepal. “No country should have to endure a catastrophe and wait seven weeks, through historic letters and relentless pressure, just to unlock the Fund’s first-ever emergency meeting. We must set up a permanent rapid-response system that moves support in days, not months,” he said. Why it is a milestone For India and other developing countries facing similar climate-induced disasters, this remains an important milestone in accessing disaster finance, experts said. Anjal Prakash, Professor of Public Policy at FLAME University and an IPCC author, said Nepal’s allocation was an important recognition of the need to pay for climate justice. “However, setting money aside is not the same as delivering it. At just 0.7% of estimated losses, this support exposes the enormous gap between climate impacts and available finance. The priority must now be rapid disbursement, with transparent safeguards that enable rather than delay assistance. We need a permanent emergency window, simpler access procedures and predictable contributions from wealthy countries,” he said, stating recovery support should reach affected families, restore essential services and protect livelihoods without adding to national debt. “Ahead of COP31, the test is delivery- whether this decision becomes a reliable system that responds to vulnerable communities at the speed and scale their losses demand, rather than another symbolic financial commitment,” he added. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Jasjeev Gandhiok Jasjeev Gandhiok is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times, where he covers environment, climate change, the clean energy transition and wildlife at the National Bureau. Gandhiok has over a decade of experience in journalism and is based in Delhi. He has reported extensively on Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR). This includes the region's air pollution woes, a polluted Yamuna and on urban wildlife still thriving in the region. He joined HT in October 2021. Prior to that, he had five-year stint at The Times of India in Delhi, where he also covered Delhi, with a focus on environment and wildlife. Gandhiok has covered some recent events around the Capital too, ranging from the farmers' protests, the northeast Delhi riots and the CAA-NRC protests, reporting from the ground on all of these. He also travels across the country to report on how environment and climate change impact everyday life, while also writing on endangered species. His reports in 2019 on toxic leachate from Delhi's landfills led to the National Green Tribunal (NGT) taking suo motu cognisance and ultimately asking the state government to start bio-mining to flatten and remove all three landfills in the capital. He also closely tracks the implementation of government policies on climate, renewable energy and environmental protection. His focus remains on impactful, public-interest journalism which explains how environmental decisions affect people's everyday lives. Read More

news.headline: CPI(M) MP Demands Independent Probe into Exposure of SBI Customer Data on Dark Web
news.story_lead: CPI(M) Member of Parliament A A Rahim has written to Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman requesting an independent investigation into the exposure of 3,897 State Bank of India customer records on the dark web. The lawmaker emphasized that even though primary banking operations remain unaffected, compromised personal financial information poses severe risks to account holders and warrants urgent institutional intervention.
news.full_article_text:
State Bank of India (SBI) formally notified the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on October 21 regarding a data security incident involving customer information. The bank disclosed that 3,897 customer records containing sensitive personal information were identified within a larger dataset of approximately 3.75 lakh records circulating on the dark web. The exposed information reportedly includes registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch details, Customer Information File (CIF) identifiers, lead IDs, and metadata associated with loan files and related records.

SBI became aware of the data breach on October 16 after receiving alerts from its threat intelligence provider, the Defence Cyber Agency, and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In). Although the state-run lender stated that its core operational systems remain completely functional and uncompromised, CPI(M) MP A A Rahim addressed a formal letter to Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on October 21 demanding urgent government action.

In his representation, MP Rahim highlighted concerns regarding cybersecurity readiness and data protection protocols across public sector banks. He asserted that the uninterrupted functioning of banking operations does not reduce the seriousness of customer privacy leaks. The MP urged the Union Finance Ministry to launch a time-bound independent investigation to identify the origin and extent of the leak, direct SBI to directly inform affected customers, establish accessible reporting channels for suspected fraud, and fix strict accountability for security lapses. He warned that affected customers could become targets for identity theft, phishing schemes, financial impersonation, and fraudulent exploitation.
bullet_points: SBI notified BSE and NSE on October 21 about a data breach involving customer information.
A total of 3,897 SBI customer records were detected on the dark web within a broader collection of 3.75 lakh records.
Compromised data includes customer names, mobile numbers, dates of birth, gender, email, residential addresses, branch codes, CIF identifiers, lead IDs, and loan metadata.
SBI learned of the incident on October 16 through alerts from its threat intelligence provider, CERT-In, and the Defence Cyber Agency.
The bank stated that its core banking operations remain unaffected by the incident.
CPI(M) MP A A Rahim wrote to Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on October 21 seeking an independent probe.
Rahim demanded direct notifications to affected account holders, setting up fraud reporting channels, and establishing strict accountability.
The lawmaker alerted that affected citizens face significant risks of identity theft, phishing, impersonation, and financial fraud.

Total dark web dataset size: Approximately 3.75 lakh records.
Stock exchanges notified: Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Date SBI learned of breach: October 16.
Informing agencies: Threat intelligence provider, CERT-In, and Defence Cyber Agency.
Date of MP's letter to FM Nirmala Sitharaman: October 21.
important_dates: October 16: SBI informed of data exposure by threat intelligence provider, CERT-In, and Defence Cyber Agency.
October 21: SBI disclosed the incident to BSE and NSE; MP A A Rahim sent representation to FM Nirmala Sitharaman.
exam_relevance: GS Paper III: Cybersecurity, Banking Infrastructure, Data Privacy, and Role of CERT-In.
Prelims: Agencies involved in cybersecurity monitoring (CERT-In, Defence Cyber Agency).
news.upsc_analysis: The incident highlights vulnerabilities in the data management frameworks of major public sector institutions. While operational continuity was maintained, the leak of granular personal data poses severe cybersecurity and fraud risks for individual account holders. It underlines the necessity for mandatory breach notification rules, robust data protection mechanisms, and comprehensive security audits across India's financial sector.
causes: Exposure of SBI customer records and loan metadata on dark web forums.
impacts: Exposure of personal data belonging to 3,897 SBI customers.
Heightened risk of identity theft, targeted phishing, financial impersonation, and fraud for affected citizens.
challenges: Securing extensive customer metadata across decentralized banking networks.
Establishing timely and transparent customer breach notification systems.
Determining breach sources when third-party vendors or file metadata are involved.
government_steps: Threat monitoring and reporting by CERT-In and Defence Cyber Agency.
SBI regulatory filings with stock exchanges (BSE and NSE).
constitutional_or_policy_link: Right to Privacy under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
Information Technology Act, 2000 and Digital Personal Data Protection Act framework.
way_forward: Conduct a time-bound independent cybersecurity audit to pinpoint the source of data exposure.
Establish direct notification protocols for affected bank account holders.
Strengthen access management controls for loan records and customer metadata across public sector banks.

SBI Data Exposure Incident:
- Details: 3,897 SBI customer records exposed on dark web out of ~3.75 lakh records.
- Timeline: SBI alerted on Oct 16 by CERT-In, Defence Cyber Agency, and threat intelligence provider; reported to BSE/NSE on Oct 21.
- Data Exposed: Names, DOB, addresses, mobile numbers, email, CIF identifiers, lead IDs, loan file metadata.
- Demands: MP A A Rahim requested FM Nirmala Sitharaman for an independent probe, direct customer notifications, fraud assistance, and accountability.
- Policy Implications: Need for mandatory breach notification standards and robust cybersecurity audits in financial sector infrastructure.

Examine the roles and coordination mechanisms between CERT-In and the Defence Cyber Agency in safeguarding national critical information infrastructure.

Defence Cyber Agency is a tri-service command of the Indian Armed Forces responsible for handling cyber threats.

hindi_translation.headline: एसबीआई ग्राहक डेटा लीक मामले में सीपीआई(एम) सांसद ने वित्त मंत्री से स्वतंत्र जांच की मांग की
hindi_translation.story_lead: सीपीआई(एम) सांसद ए ए रहीम ने केंद्रीय वित्त मंत्री निर्मला सीतारमण को पत्र लिखकर डार्क वेब पर भारतीय स्टेट बैंक के 3,897 ग्राहकों के रिकॉर्ड उजागर होने की स्वतंत्र जांच की मांग की है। सांसद ने जोर दिया कि भले ही मुख्य बैंकिंग परिचालन अप्रभावित रहे हों, लेकिन व्यक्तिगत वित्तीय जानकारी के लीक होने से ग्राहकों के लिए गंभीर जोखिम पैदा होता है और इसके लिए तत्काल संस्थागत कदम उठाने की आवश्यकता है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
भारतीय स्टेट बैंक (एसबीआई) ने 21 अक्टूबर को बॉम्बे स्टॉक एक्सचेंज (बीएसई) और नेशनल स्टॉक एक्सचेंज (एनएसई) को ग्राहक डेटा से जुड़ी एक सुरक्षा घटना की औपचारिक जानकारी दी। बैंक ने खुलासा किया कि डार्क वेब पर घूम रहे लगभग 3.75 लाख रिकॉर्ड्स के एक बड़े सेट में 3,897 एसबीआई ग्राहक रिकॉर्ड पाए गए जिनमें संवेदनशील व्यक्तिगत जानकारी शामिल थी। उजागर हुई जानकारी में पंजीकृत मोबाइल नंबर, जन्म तिथि, नाम, लिंग, ईमेल पते, आवासीय पते, शाखा विवरण, ग्राहक सूचना फाइल (सीआईएफ) पहचानकर्ता, लीड आईडी और ऋण रिकॉर्ड से जुड़े मेटाडेटा शामिल बताए गए हैं।

एसबीआई को 16 अक्टूबर को प्रदाता थ्रेट इंटेलिजेंस, डिफेंस साइबर एजेंसी और इंडियन कंप्यूटर इमरजेंसी रिस्पॉन्स टीम (सीईआरटी-इन) से अलर्ट मिलने के बाद इस डेटा लीक का पता चला। यद्यपि सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के इस बैंक ने कहा कि उसका मुख्य बैंकिंग परिचालन पूरी तरह से सुरक्षित और अप्रभावित रहा, सीपीआई(एम) सांसद ए ए रहीम ने 21 अक्टूबर को वित्त मंत्री निर्मला सीतारमण को पत्र भेजकर तत्काल सरकारी हस्तक्षेप की मांग की।

अपने पत्र में सांसद रहीम ने सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के बैंकों में साइबर सुरक्षा तैयारियों और डेटा सुरक्षा प्रोटोकॉल को लेकर चिंता व्यक्त की। उन्होंने तर्क दिया कि बैंकिंग सेवाओं में व्यवधान न आने से ग्राहकों की व्यक्तिगत जानकारी के उजागर होने की गंभीरता कम नहीं हो जाती। सांसद ने वित्त मंत्रालय से मांग की कि वह इस लीक के स्रोत और सीमा की पहचान के लिए समयबद्ध स्वतंत्र जांच कराए, एसबीआई को सीधे प्रभावित ग्राहकों को सूचित करने का निर्देश दे, संदिग्ध धोखाधड़ी की रिपोर्टिंग के लिए सुलभ चैनल स्थापित करे और सुरक्षा चूक के लिए कड़ी जवाबदेही तय करे। उन्होंने चेतावनी दी कि प्रभावित ग्राहक पहचान की चोरी, लक्षित फ़िशिंग, वित्तीय धोखाधड़ी और शोषण का शिकार हो सकते हैं।
bullet_points: एसबीआई ने 21 अक्टूबर को बीएसई और एनएसई को ग्राहक डेटा सुरक्षा घटना के बारे में सूचित किया।
डार्क वेब पर 3.75 लाख रिकॉर्ड के बड़े सेट में एसबीआई के 3,897 ग्राहक रिकॉर्ड की पहचान की गई।
लीक हुए डेटा में नाम, मोबाइल नंबर, जन्म तिथि, लिंग, ईमेल, आवासीय पता, सीआईएफ आईडी और लोन मेटाडेटा शामिल हैं।
एसबीआई को 16 अक्टूबर को सीईआरटी-इन, डिफेंस साइबर एजेंसी और थ्रेट इंटेलिजेंस प्रदाता से घटना की जानकारी मिली।
बैंक ने स्पष्ट किया कि उसके मुख्य बैंकिंग परिचालन पर कोई प्रभाव नहीं पड़ा है।
सीपीआई(एम) सांसद ए ए रहीम ने 21 अक्टूबर को वित्त मंत्री निर्मला सीतारमण को स्वतंत्र जांच के लिए पत्र लिखा।
रहीम ने प्रभावित ग्राहकों को सीधी सूचना देने, धोखाधड़ी रिपोर्टिंग चैनल स्थापित करने और सख्त जवाबदेही तय करने की मांग की।
सांसद ने चेतावनी दी कि प्रभावित नागरिक पहचान की चोरी, फ़िशिंग और वित्तीय धोखाधड़ी के खतरे में हैं।

डार्क वेब डेटासेट का कुल आकार: लगभग 3.75 लाख रिकॉर्ड।
अधिसूचित स्टॉक एक्सचेंज: बीएसई और एनएसई।

news.headline: Kolkata Durga Puja Stampede: SIT Identifies Narrow Exits and Dim Lighting as Primary Triggers
news.story_lead: A six-member Special Investigation Team (SIT) investigating the fatal October 17 Durga Puja stampede in Kolkata has identified severe crowd-flow bottlenecks, inadequate lighting, and false loudspeaker announcements as core factors behind the tragedy. The incident at the Chor Bagan pandal resulted in 19 deaths and left 25 individuals injured on the Saptami day of the festival. Police have detained eight individuals under key provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
news.full_article_text:
A six-member Special Investigation Team (SIT), headed by retired Calcutta High Court judge Anindita Roy Saraswati, has identified structural bottlenecks and operational lapses as key factors behind the October 17 stampede at the Chor Bagan Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata. The tragedy took place on Saptami, the seventh day of the festival, claiming 19 lives and injuring 25 people during heavy rainfall and intense crowd surging.

Preliminary findings by the SIT confirm that the stampede occurred at the exit point rather than inside the pandal itself. Investigators highlighted that common visitors were funneled into a single, dimly lit exit pathway measuring approximately seven feet in width. This egress route was further constricted by installed outdoor air conditioning compressor units and temporary food stalls along the lane. Furthermore, access to the primary view of the idol required visitors to navigate a five-foot-wide circular ramp, which lacked alternative evacuation routes.

Witness reports and police findings indicate that the emergency gate, typically designated for VIP movement, remained locked during the surge. The immediate trigger for the stampede appears to have been an unverified announcement over the public address system claiming that the pandal structure was collapsing, prompting widespread panic among the crowd trying to descend from the ramp.

Law enforcement officials have taken eight individuals into custody in connection with the incident, including puja committee secretary Raj Kumar Sewda, vice-president Santanu Dubey, and committee member Sanjib Raha, who was identified as one of the individuals who made the panicky announcement over the loudspeaker. All accused have been charged under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) Sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder), 110 (attempt to commit culpable homicide), and 3(5) (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention). Seven of the accused were remanded to 10-day police custody.

To recreate the scene and establish accountability, police forensic teams conducted 3D spatial mapping and deployed drone aerial surveillance around the pandal and adjacent narrow lanes. The incident has also sparked a political controversy in West Bengal, with opposition parties criticizing the administration and pointing to political figures associated as patrons with the event management committee. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari visited the affected families, announcing financial compensation and a state government employment pledge for one family member of each deceased victim.
news.background_context: West Bengal has no recent history of fatal stampedes occurring at Durga Puja pandals, making the October 17 tragedy at Chor Bagan an unprecedented crowd management crisis during the state's largest cultural festival.
bullet_points: A 6-member SIT led by retired Judge Anindita Roy Saraswati is investigating the Chor Bagan pandal stampede.
The tragedy on Saptami (October 17) resulted in 19 fatalities and 25 injuries.
Investigations reveal the stampede happened at a narrow 7-foot exit pathway constrained by AC units and food stalls.
Emergency VIP exit gates were reportedly kept locked, leaving visitors with no secondary escape route.
Panicked crowds rushed after a false announcement was made over the public address system claiming structural collapse.
Eight people have been arrested or detained, including key members of the puja organizing committee.
Charges have been invoked under BNS Sections 105, 110, and 3(5).
Forensic teams utilized drone surveillance and 3D mapping to analyze the physical layout of the venue.
The West Bengal government announced financial compensation and a government job for a family member of each victim.

SIT led by retired Calcutta High Court Judge Anindita Roy Saraswati.
Exit path width was approximately 7 feet, narrowed further by AC units and stalls.
360-degree viewing ramp dimensions: 5 feet wide and 7 feet high.

key_locations: Chor Bagan, North Kolkata, West Bengal
important_dates: 2026-10-17: Stampede occurred on Saptami day of Durga Puja
2026-10-23: Eighth accused produced in court following arrest
exam_relevance: UPSC Mains GS-3: Disaster Management and infrastructure safety in mass public gatherings.
UPSC Mains GS-2: Public administration, regulatory compliance, and government oversight.
Prelims: Application of BNS sections and institutional mechanisms like Special Investigation Teams.
news.upsc_analysis: The Kolkata Durga Puja stampede underscores persistent gaps in urban crowd management, structural audit protocols, and event administration during mass religious gatherings in high-density urban areas. Key failure points identified—such as constrained egress points, single-point entry/exit designs, locked emergency gates, and panic dissemination via unauthorized public address announcements—highlight the need for strict adherence to National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) guidelines on mass gatherings. The incident emphasizes that technical planning (like dynamic spatial mapping and emergency evacuation routes) must be legally enforced alongside administrative accountability.
causes: Severely restricted 7-foot exit pathway further obstructed by food stalls and AC compressor units.
Absence of secondary emergency exit options due to locked VIP gates.
Dimly lit egress routes causing reduced visibility during mass dispersion.
Rumour mongering and misleading loudspeaker announcements regarding structural collapse.
impacts: Loss of 19 lives and injuries to 25 attendees.
Police proceedings against organizers under criminal provisions of BNS.
Heightened scrutiny on safety clearances for mass cultural events.
challenges: Managing high crowd densities in narrow, legacy urban streets of north Kolkata.
Enforcing strict safety and structural clearances on temporary festival structures.
Preventing panic spread caused by unverified public announcements.
government_steps: Constituted a 6-member SIT headed by a retired High Court Judge.
Deployed forensic teams for 3D mapping and drone-assisted spatial inspection.
Initiated criminal prosecution under BNS Sections 105, 110, and 3(5).
Extended monetary relief and state employment assistance to affected families.
constitutional_or_policy_link: NDMA Guidelines on Managing Crowds at Places of Mass Gathering
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) provisions governing culpable homicide and common intention
way_forward: Mandate structural and crowd-flow safety audits prior to issuing festival permits.
Ensure mandatory dual exit routes and functional emergency doors for all temporary public venues.
Establish strict protocols and trained personnel control over public address systems during large events.
news.mains_notes: Crowd management at major public events requires systematic compliance with safety norms. Key elements include structural stability checks, clear demarcated entry and exit pathways, dedicated emergency egress lanes, and standardized communication protocols to prevent panic. Institutionalizing NDMA guidelines at municipal and police district levels is critical to preventing stampede tragedies.
mains_questions: Examine the primary infrastructural and administrative factors contributing to crowd stampedes during mass cultural events in India. Suggest corrective measures based on NDMA guidelines.
How can local administration leverage technology and rigid regulatory frameworks to prevent human-error-induced panics at high-density public venues?
news.takeaway: The Kolkata Durga Puja stampede tragedy highlights critical regulatory and administrative failures in crowd flow design, emergency access, and rumor control during major public gatherings.
prelims_facts: BNS Section 105 covers culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
BNS Section 110 relates to attempt to commit culpable homicide.
BNS Section 3(5) deals with acts performed by multiple individuals with common intention.

hindi_translation.headline: कोलकाता दुर्गा पूजा भगदड़: एसआईटी ने संकीर्ण निकास और कम रोशनी को मुख्य कारण बताया
hindi_translation.story_lead: कोलकाता के चोर बगान पंडाल में 17 अक्टूबर को हुई घातक दुर्गा पूजा भगदड़ की जांच कर रही छह सदस्यीय विशेष जांच टीम (SIT) ने भीड़ नियंत्रण की कमियों, अपर्याप्त रोशनी और लाउडस्पीकर से की गई झूठी घोषणाओं को इस त्रासदी का मुख्य कारण माना है। सप्तमी के दिन हुई इस घटना में 19 लोगों की मौत हो गई थी और 25 लोग घायल हुए थे। पुलिस ने भारतीय न्याय संहिता (BNS) की धाराओं के तहत आठ लोगों को हिरासत में लिया है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
कलकत्ता उच्च न्यायालय की सेवानिवृत्त न्यायाधीश अनिंदिता रॉय सरस्वती के नेतृत्व में छह सदस्यीय विशेष जांच टीम (SIT) ने उत्तर कोलकाता के चोर बगान दुर्गा पूजा पंडाल में 17 अक्टूबर को हुई भगदड़ के पीछे ढांचागत कमियों और परिचालनगत चूक की पहचान की है। यह हादसा त्यौहार के सातवें दिन (सप्तमी) को भारी बारिश और भीड़ के दबाव के दौरान हुआ, जिसमें 19 लोगों की जान चली गई और 25 अन्य घायल हो गए।

एसआईटी के शुरुआती निष्कर्षों से पुष्टि होती है कि भगदड़ पंडाल के अंदर नहीं बल्कि निकास बिंदु पर हुई थी। जांचकर्ताओं ने पाया कि आम आगंतुकों को लगभग सात फीट चौड़े और कम रोशनी वाले एक ही निकास मार्ग से निकाला जा रहा था। पंडाल के भीतर लगी एयर कंडीशनर मशीनों की बाहरी इकाइयों और सड़क पर लगी खाद्य दुकानों के कारण यह निकास मार्ग और अधिक संकरा हो गया था। इसके अलावा, मूर्ति के 360-डिग्री दर्शन के लिए पांच फीट चौड़े और सात फीट ऊंचे गोलाकार रैंप से गुजरना पड़ता था, जहां से बाहर निकलने का कोई वैकल्पिक रास्ता नहीं था।

प्रत्यक्षदर्शियों और पुलिस जांच के अनुसार, वीआईपी आवाजाही के लिए इस्तेमाल होने वाला आपातकालीन गेट घटना के दौरान बंद था। भगदड़ की तात्कालिक वजह लाउडस्पीकर के माध्यम से की गई एक अप्रमाणित घोषणा बनी, जिसमें दावा किया गया था कि पंडाल का ढांचा ढहने वाला है। इस घोषणा से रैंप पर मौजूद लोगों में दहशत फैल गई और वे जान बचाने के लिए भागने लगे।

पुलिस ने इस मामले में आठ लोगों को गिरफ्तार या हिरासत में लिया है, जिनमें पूजा समिति के सचिव राज कुमार सेवड़ा, उपाध्यक्ष शांतनु दुबे और समिति सदस्य संजीब राहा शामिल हैं। संजीब राहा पर लाउडस्पीकर से घबराहट फैलाने वाली घोषणा करने का आरोप है। सभी आरोपियों पर भारतीय न्याय संहिता (BNS) की धारा 105 (गैर-इरादतन हत्या), 110 (गैर-इरादतन हत्या का प्रयास) और 3(5) (समान मंशा से किया गया अपराध) के तहत मामला दर्ज किया गया है। सात आरोपियों को 10 दिनों की पुलिस हिरासत में भेज दिया गया है।

घटनास्थल के पुनर्निर्माण और जिम्मेदारी तय करने के लिए, पुलिस फोरेंसिक टीमों ने 3D मैपिंग की और ड्रोन कैमरों से पंडाल और आसपास की संकरी गलियों का हवाई सर्वेक्षण किया। इस घटना ने पश्चिम बंगाल में राजनीतिक विवाद भी खड़ा कर दिया है। राज्य के मुख्यमंत्री शुभेंदु अधिकारी ने पीड़ित परिवारों से मुलाकात की और प्रत्येक मृतक के परिवार के एक सदस्य को राज्य सरकार में नौकरी और वित्तीय मुआवजे का वादा किया है।
hindi_translation.background_context: पश्चिम बंगाल में दुर्गा पूजा पंडालों में भगदड़ से मौत की कोई हालिया इतिहास नहीं रही है, जिसके कारण चोर बगान की यह घटना राज्य के सबसे बड़े सांस्कृतिक उत्सव के दौरान एक अभूतपूर्व भीड़ प्रबंधन संकट बन गई है।
bullet_points: सेवानिवृत्त न्यायाधीश अनिंदिता रॉय सरस्वती के नेतृत्व में 6 सदस्यीय एसआईटी चोर बगान पंडाल भगदड़ की जांच कर रही है।
17 अक्टूबर (सप्तमी) को हुई इस त्रासदी में 19 लोगों की मौत हुई और 25 घायल हुए।
जांच से पता चला है कि भगदड़ संकीर्ण 7-फीट निकास मार्ग पर हुई, जो दुकानों और एसी इकाइयों से घिरा था।
वीआईपी आपातकालीन गेट बंद रखा गया था, जिससे आगंतुकों के पास बाहर निकलने का कोई दूसरा रास्ता नहीं था।
लाउडस्पीकर पर ढांचा ढहने की झूठी अफवाह के बाद भीड़ में भगदड़ मच गई।
पूजा आयोजक समिति के प्रमुख सदस्यों सहित आठ लोगों को गिरफ्तार/हिरासत में लिया गया है।
आरोपियों पर बीएनएस की धारा 105, 110 और 3(5) के तहत मामले दर्ज किए गए हैं।
फोरेंसिक टीम ने 3D मैपिंग और ड्रोन कैमरों से स्थल का विश्लेषण किया।

news.exam_corner_topic: Serbia Snap Parliamentary Elections and Civic Movement
static_gk: Parliamentary Structure: National Assembly (Unicameral legislature with 250 seats)
Electoral System: Party-list proportional representation with a single national constituency and a 3% electoral threshold
news.headline: Civic Movement Led by 'Student List' Challenges 12-Year Rule of Aleksandar Vučić in Serbia
news.story_lead: Serbia is conducting snap parliamentary elections following two years of widespread anti-government protests triggered by a fatal infrastructure collapse in Novi Sad. Long-serving leader Aleksandar Vučić faces a significant political challenge from the 'Student List-Students Win' civic movement, which unites diverse socio-professional groups despite concerns over electoral fairness and state media bias.
news.full_article_text:
### Electoral Context and Political Landscape
Serbia's political landscape faces a critical turning point as citizens prepare for snap parliamentary elections. The election serves as a pivotal juncture for President Aleksandar Vučić, who has dominated Serbian politics for 12 years as Prime Minister, President, or Deputy Prime Minister since 2012. Having completed two terms as president, Vučić is leading his ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) with the goal of regaining the Prime Minister's office.

### Genesis of the Protests: The Novi Sad Tragedy
The political momentum shifted on 1 November 2024 when a concrete canopy collapsed at the railway station in Novi Sad, Serbia's second-largest city, resulting in 16 deaths. Public outrage focused on allegations of systemic corruption, official negligence, and poor oversight linked to the station's renovation project. The incident sparked student-led campus and street demonstrations, which subsequently expanded into a national civic movement involving farmers, actors, judges, and academics, organized via decentralized student plenums.

### Electoral System and Key Candidates
Serbia's legislative framework operates as a single national constituency with 250 parliamentary seats chosen under proportional representation with a 3% threshold. Out of 18 contesting lists, 7 are running a complete candidate slate for the 6.45 million registered voters.

The prominent opposition force, 'Student List-Students Win', features a non-partisan roster of professionals rather than active students. Key candidates include lead candidate Dr. Ilija Srdanović (a cardiology professor from Novi Sad), Dejan Bodiroga (former basketball player), Tihomir Stanić (actor), and Dejan Šoškić (former Governor of the National Bank of Serbia).

### Platform and Integrity Issues
The Student List's 11-point platform focuses on creating a specialized anti-corruption police unit, purging ministry officials linked to abuses or organized crime, ensuring public broadcast neutrality, and stopping political appointments in state enterprises. Independent observers, including CRTA and the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE), have cited media imbalances, electoral engineering, and over 160 reported attacks on media workers during the year.
news.background_context: On 1 November 2024, a concrete canopy collapsed at the Novi Sad train station in Serbia, causing 16 deaths. The tragedy catalyzed anti-government protests against state corruption and administrative negligence, eventually causing the prime minister's resignation and large-scale demonstrations in Belgrade in March 2025.
bullet_points: Serbia holds snap elections to fill 250 seats in its unicameral National Assembly.
Aleksandar Vučić, ruling for 12 years, seeks a return to the Prime Minister's post after completing two presidential terms.
The 'Student List-Students Win' movement emerged after the 1 November 2024 Novi Sad train station canopy collapse that killed 16 people.
The opposition list features prominent professionals including cardiologist Ilija Srdanović, actor Tihomir Stanić, ex-basketball player Dejan Bodiroga, and former central bank governor Dejan Šoškić.
The Student List program focuses on anti-corruption enforcement, media independence, reform of public appointments, and police accountability.
Elections use a single national constituency with a 3% electoral threshold under proportional representation.
Independent monitor CRTA reported electoral engineering and nearly 75% state media bias toward government representatives.
The European Centre for Press and Media Freedom logged around 160 attacks on media personnel in Serbia during the current year.

It highlights the role of non-partisan civic slates in challenging entrenched political dominance, while illustrating the challenges posed by uneven media access, state resource utilization, and institutional bias during electoral processes in hybrid democracies.

Proportional representation models and electoral threshold mechanisms in parliamentary democracies.
way_forward: Ensure complete independence of media regulators and public broadasting networks.
Strengthen non-partisan election monitoring bodies to prevent electoral engineering.
Implement transparent procurement and accountability standards for public infrastructure projects to restore public trust.

hindi_translation.headline: 'स्टूडेंट लिस्ट' के नेतृत्व में नागरिक आंदोलन ने सर्बिया में अलेक्जेंडर वुचिच के 12 साल के शासन को चुनौती दी
hindi_translation.story_lead: नोवी साद में एक दुखद बुनियादी ढांचा दुर्घटना के बाद शुरू हुए दो साल के विरोध प्रदर्शनों के बाद सर्बिया में मध्यावधि संसदीय चुनाव हो रहे हैं। सर्बिया के दीर्घकालिक नेता अलेक्जेंडर वुचिच को 'स्टूडेंट लिस्ट-स्टूडेंट्स विन' आंदोलन से कड़ी चुनौती मिल रही है, जो निष्पक्षता और मीडिया पक्षपात की चिंताओं के बीच विभिन्न नागरिक वर्गों को एकजुट करता है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### चुनावी पृष्ठभूमि और राजनीतिक परिदृश्य
सर्बिया का राजनीतिक परिदृश्य एक महत्वपूर्ण मोड़ पर पहुंच गया है क्योंकि नागरिक मध्यावधि संसदीय चुनावों के लिए मतदान करने जा रहे हैं। यह चुनाव राष्ट्रपति अलेक्जेंडर वुचिच के लिए एक महत्वपूर्ण परीक्षा है, जिन्होंने 2012 से प्रधानमंत्री, राष्ट्रपति या उप-प्रधानमंत्री के रूप में 12 वर्षों तक सर्बियाई राजनीति पर वर्चस्व बनाए रखा है। राष्ट्रपति के रूप में दो कार्यकाल पूरे करने के बाद, वुचिच अपनी सत्तारूढ़ सर्बियन प्रोग्रेसिव पार्टी (SNS) का नेतृत्व प्रधानमंत्री पद पर लौटने के उद्देश्य से कर रहे हैं।

### विरोध प्रदर्शनों की शुरुआत: नोवी साद दुर्घटना
1 नवंबर 2024 को सर्बिया के दूसरे सबसे बड़े शहर नोवी साद में रेलवे स्टेशन की कंक्रीट शेड गिरने से 16 लोगों की मौत हो गई, जिसने राजनीतिक माहौल को बदल दिया। जन आक्रोश ने स्टेशन के नवीनीकरण से जुड़े भ्रष्टाचार और लापरवाही पर ध्यान केंद्रित किया। इस घटना ने विश्वविद्यालय परिसरों और सड़कों पर प्रदर्शनों को जन्म दिया, जो बाद में किसानों, अभिनेताओं, न्यायाधीशों और शिक्षाविदों को शामिल करते हुए एक व्यापक राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन में बदल गया।

### चुनावी प्रणाली और प्रमुख उम्मीदवार
सर्बिया की विधायी प्रणाली में 250 संसदीय सीटें हैं, जो 3% सीमा के साथ आनुपातिक प्रतिनिधित्व के तहत चुनी जाती हैं। 64.5 लाख पंजीकृत मतदाताओं के लिए चुनाव लड़ रही 18 सूचियों में से केवल 7 ने पूर्ण 250 उम्मीदवारों की सूची पेश की है।

विपक्षी बल 'स्टूडेंट लिस्ट' में सक्रिय छात्रों के बजाय पेशेवर शामिल हैं। प्रमुख उम्मीदवारों में डॉक्टर इलिजा सर्डानोविच (नोवी साद के कार्डियोलॉजी प्रोफेसर), देजान बोडिरोगा (पूर्व बास्केटबॉल खिलाड़ी), तिहोमिर स्टेनिच (अभिनेता) और देजान शोश्किच (नेशनल बैंक ऑफ सर्बिया के पूर्व गवर्नर) शामिल हैं।

### मंच और निष्पक्षता से जुड़े मुद्दे
स्टूडेंट लिस्ट का 11-सूत्रीय कार्यक्रम भ्रष्टाचार विरोधी पुलिस इकाई के गठन, अनुचित कार्रवाई या संगठित अपराध में शामिल अधिकारियों को हटाने और सार्वजनिक प्रसारण में निष्पक्षता बहाल करने पर केंद्रित है। सीआरटीए और काउंसिल ऑफ यूरोप (पेस) जैसे स्वतंत्र पर्यवेक्षकों ने मीडिया असमानता, चुनावी हेरफेर और पत्रकारों पर 160 से अधिक हमलों की रिपोर्ट दी है।
hindi_translation.background_context: 1 नवंबर 2024 को सर्बिया के नोवी साद ट्रेन स्टेशन पर कंक्रीट की छत गिरने से 16 लोगों की मृत्यु हो गई थी। इस दुर्घटना ने भ्रष्टाचार और प्रशासनिक लापरवाही के खिलाफ व्यापक जन आंदोलन को जन्म दिया, जिससे प्रधानमंत्री को इस्तीफा देना पड़ा।

12 साल से सत्ता में मौजूद अलेक्जेंडर वुचिच राष्ट्रपति पद के दो कार्यकाल के बाद फिर से प्रधानमंत्री बनने की कोशिश में हैं।
1 नवंबर 2024 को नोवी साद रेलवे स्टेशन की छत गिरने से 16 लोगों की मौत के बाद 'स्टूडेंट लिस्ट' आंदोलन की शुरुआत हुई।
विपक्षी उम्मीदवार सूची में कार्डियोलॉजिस्ट इलिजा सर्डानोविच, अभिनेता तिहोमिर स्टेनिच, पूर्व बास्केटबॉल खिलाड़ी देजान बोडिरोगा और पूर्व केंद्रीय बैंक गवर्नर देजान शोश्किच शामिल हैं।
स्टूडेंट लिस्ट का 11-सूत्रीय एजेंडा भ्रष्टाचार विरोधी पुलिस बल, मीडिया स्वतंत्रता और पुलिस जवाबदेही पर केंद्रित है।
चुनाव आनुपातिक प्रतिनिधित्व प्रणाली के तहत 3% की न्यूनतम सीमा के साथ आयोजित किए जाते हैं।
स्वतंत्र निगरानी संस्था CRTA ने मीडिया में लगभग 75% सरकारी कवरेज और चुनावी हेरफेर की बात कही है।
यूरोपीय प्रेस और मीडिया स्वतंत्रता केंद्र ने चालू वर्ष में सर्बिया में पत्रकारों पर लगभग 160 हमलों को दर्ज किया।

news.exam_corner_topic: RTI Disclosure on Election Commission Administrative Complaints
static_gk: Election Commission of India: A constitutional body established under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution responsible for administering election processes in India.
Cabinet Secretariat: Functions under the direct charge of the Prime Minister of India, providing administrative support and coordination across government ministries.
news.headline: Cabinet Secretariat Took No Action on Complaint by Two Election Commissioners Against Poll Panel Official: RTI
news.story_lead: A disclosure under the Right to Information (RTI) Act revealed that two Election Commissioners had formally complained against an officer within the Election Commission. Despite acknowledgment of the complaints by the Cabinet Secretary, the Cabinet Secretariat did not initiate administrative action on the matter.
news.full_article_text:
### Administrative Oversight and RTI Disclosure

Information obtained through a Right to Information (RTI) application reveals that two Election Commissioners filed formal complaints regarding a poll panel officer. The disclosures indicate that while the complaints were received and acknowledged by the Cabinet Secretariat, no administrative or disciplinary steps were taken following the submission.

- **Key Event**: Two Election Commissioners submitted complaints against an officer within the poll body.
- **Secretariat Response**: The Cabinet Secretary officially acknowledged the receipt of the written complaints.
- **Outcome**: The RTI disclosure confirms that the Cabinet Secretariat refrained from initiating action regarding the allegations made by the commissioners.

This development brings attention to inter-institutional communication and grievance mechanisms within executive and constitutional oversight bodies in India.
bullet_points: An RTI query disclosed that two Election Commissioners registered complaints against an official within the Election Commission of India.
The Cabinet Secretary officially acknowledged receiving the grievances filed by the commissioners.
The Cabinet Secretariat took no administrative action in response to the filed complaints.
The findings were brought to light through a public records request under the Right to Information Act.
The situation underscores questions regarding administrative oversight and institutional complaint resolution processes.
key_facts: Two Election Commissioners filed official complaints against a poll panel officer.
The Cabinet Secretariat acknowledged receipt of the complaints.
No administrative action was taken by the Cabinet Secretariat, as confirmed by an RTI response.
important_dates: October 23, 2026: Date of publication reporting the RTI findings regarding the poll panel officer complaints.
exam_relevance: Relevant for UPSC GS Paper II under Constitutional Bodies (Election Commission of India), Structure and Functioning of the Executive (Cabinet Secretariat), and Accountability mechanisms (RTI Act).
news.upsc_analysis: The disclosure highlights administrative interactions between constitutional bodies like the Election Commission of India and executive organs such as the Cabinet Secretariat. It emphasizes the importance of clear procedures for handling administrative grievances within statutory and constitutional frameworks to maintain institutional integrity.
causes: Complaints submitted by two Election Commissioners against an officer serving within the election body.
impacts: Increased public scrutiny regarding the handling of internal administrative complaints within constitutional agencies.
challenges: Ensuring transparent administrative procedures and swift resolution of grievances involving high-level officers and constitutional authorities.
government_steps: Receipt and acknowledgment of internal complaints by the Cabinet Secretariat.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Article 324 of the Constitution of India relating to the powers and functioning of the Election Commission of India.
Right to Information Act, 2005 governing access to public records.
way_forward: Establishing clear standard operating procedures for investigating administrative grievances within constitutional bodies to uphold transparency and administrative efficiency.
news.mains_notes: Key aspects for Mains examination include the constitutional status and autonomy of the Election Commission under Article 324, the role of the Cabinet Secretariat in administrative coordination, and the utility of the RTI Act as a tool for public accountability.
mains_questions: Examine the constitutional safeguards provided to the Election Commission of India to ensure its autonomous functioning, and discuss how administrative grievances should be systematically addressed.
Analyze the role of the Right to Information (RTI) Act in bringing transparency to inter-departmental operations in governance.
news.takeaway: An RTI response revealed that the Cabinet Secretariat took no action after receiving complaints from two Election Commissioners regarding a poll panel officer.
